main_text.l: ORITHYA, Marthesiæ filia, Amazonum post matrem
Regina, tum ob belli industriam, tum ob perpetuam virginita-
tem, conspicuam se, ac mirabilem præstitit. Hæc vbi coperit bel-
lum, vim quoque sororibus suis illatam ab Hercule & Theseo,
hortatur comites in vltionē, frustráque Ponti sinum & Asiam
domitam esse dicit, si Græcorum non tam bellis quàm rapinis
pateant. auxiliū à Rege Scytharum capit. Sed ante prœliū dis-
sensione orta, ab auxiliis desertæ Amazones, bellóq; ab Athe-
niésibus victæ, receptaculum tamen habuere castra sociorum,
in regnúmque reuersæ sunt. Iustin. lib. 2.
PENTHESILEA post Orythiam Amazonis impera-
uit. Hæc Troianis aduersus Græcos opem tulit. Verg. lib. Aen. 1.
Ducit Amazonidum lunatis agmina peltis
Penthesilea furens, mediisque in millibus ardet,
Aurea subnectens exerta cingula mamma
Bellatrix, audétque viris concurrere virgo.
Interfecta demum ab Achille, exercitúque eius absumpto,
paucæ quæ remanserant vsque ad tempora Alexandri Magni
durauerunt: quem Thalestris, Amazonum Regina, adiit, ad so-
bolem ex eo generandam. Hunc cum ter centum feminis salu-
tauit, cæteris iussis subsistere, copiam sui fecit ei Alexander per
tredecim dies. Hæc coram illi in os ingenuè fassa est se tantum
ad suscipiēdos liberos venisse: fœminini sexus se retenturam,
marem patri redditurā. reuersa in regnum, breui pòst tempore
cum omni Amazonum nomine intercidit. Quint. Curt. lib. 6.
Iustin. lib. 2. de hac vide etiam infra in Alexandro.

main_text.l: MENELAVS REX SPAR.
AGMEMNON REX MYC[?]
MENELAVS, Atrei (alij dicunt Plisthenis) & Aeropes
filius, in uxorem accepit Helenam formosissimā quidem mu-
lierem, attamē quæ bis rapta est, primùm à Thefeo, postea à Pa-
ride. Hic Menelaus regnauit apud Lacedæmonios anno mundi
2758. ante Christum natum 1204. aduersus Troianos bel-
lum gessit pro recuperanda uxore, quam non nisi capta Troia
recuperauit. bellum gessit decem fere annis. præterea conscen-
dens nauim in reditu, non nisi post octauum erroris annum pa-
triam attigit. Tantæ molis erat infame reducere scortū. scribit
nihilominus Dictys Cretensis non tam animo consternatum
fuisse Menelaum ob raptam uxorem, quàm ob Aetram & Cly-
menam, affines suas. Sustulit ex Helena Hermionem. Dares
Phry. Ouid. lib. 11. Metamorp. Cæterùm Menelaum Atrei fi-
lium Homerus scribit, Hesiodus autem, Plisthenis.
AGAMEMNON regnauit Mycœnis anno mundi
2768. ante Christum natum 1194. hic frater fuit Menelai: &
omnium consensu Græcorum dux præcipuus aduersus Troia-
nos declaratus est: classem habuit nauium sexaginta supra cen-
tum: uniuersa Græcorum classis erat nauium plus mille. Tan-
dem reuersus ab expeditione illa, & bello Troiano confecto,
ipse, insidiis Clytemestræ uxoris, ab Aegystho adultero interfi-
citur: Orestésque filius eius hanc iniuriā ulcisci-tur, interfectis
adulteris, matre scilicet Clytemnestra ac Aegystho. Euripid. in
Oreste, Seneca in Agamemnone. Dares Phrygi. Dictys Cre.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are copied from the engraved rings. The right legend is partly hidden by the curve of the medallion: "AGMEMNON" and "REX MYC" are my reading, and the end of the word is uncertain. Paragraph 1: "Clytemestræ" (paragraph 2) and "Clytenestræ" are the same name as printed. Some letters in the scan are faint, but the running text reads cleanly. No notes in the margins.

page.layout: Top: printed page number at left and running head centred. Below them, two round medallion woodcuts side by side, each with a marginal legend. Below the woodcuts, one column of text at full width, in two paragraphs. No margin notes.

main_text.l: PARIS. ALEXAN.
HELENA
PARIS, qui & Alexander dictus, Priami filius fuit & He-
cubæ. Hunc pater exponi iussit, quòd mater prægnans somnias-
set se facem ardentem parere: attamen Hecuba materno asse-
ctu ducta, curauit ut in Ida monte à pastoribus nutriretur. Adole-
scens Oenonem amauit, ex qua Idæum & Daphnidem sustulit.
Tandem à parentibus agnitus ac receptus, suscepit legationem
in Græciam ad repetendam Hesionem, ubi Helenam rapuit,
Troiamque abduxit anno mundi 2768. ante Christum natum
1194. nempe primo anno regni Agamemnonis. Propterea
bellum Græcorum aduersus Troianos exarsit. Scribit Herodo-
tus renitentem abduxisse, Spartenque expugnasse, ob id à viro
recipi meruisse. Achillē sagitta interemit Paris, vicissim quoq;
interemptus est à Pyrrho Achillis filio. Herodo. lib. 2. Dares,
Dictys Cretensis.
HELENA, Jouis & Ledæ filia, à Thefeo primùm rapta,
nec multo post Castori & Polluci fratribus reddita, Menelai
uxor fuit, cui Hermionem peperit: hanc Paris seu volentem seu
nolentem abduxit, uti dictum à me supra est, ac in uxorem du-
xit. Hæc proditionis Troiæ cōscia fuisse dicitur, cum Greci ar-
mis diffidentes ad dolum se cōuertissent: ac facem, proditionis
signum, ex arce sustulisse, & cum priore viro in gratiâ rediisse.
De simulachro ac templo Helenæ, in quo mulier ex turpissima,
speciosissima facta est, vide Herodotum libr. 6. Capta est Troia
deficiente jam vere, 17. diebus ante conuersionem æstiuam, an-
no mundi 2783. ante Christum natum 1179. Vide Dionys.
Halicar.

page.notes: Two round woodcut medallions with portrait busts in profile: the left one shows a bearded man in a helmet, the right one a woman with a decorated headdress. Legends are printed around the medallions as shown in main_text. Printed page number and running head are at the top. Old-style figures in the dates are set with spaces between digits in print; given here without spaces. Long s is read as plain s. Reading of "Achillē" is taken from a tilde-marked e, uncertain. No doubtful words otherwise.

page.layout: Full-width page top: running head at top centre, page number at top right. Below it, two round medallion portraits side by side, each with a legend around its edge. Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs. Below the text, at the right, a signature mark. Lower down, a woodcut ornament, which is not text.

main_text.l: GRECVS ULYSSES.
PENELOPE ULY.CON.[?]
ULYSSES Laërtæ & Anticliæ filius, Solers ac disertus
extitit, atque prudentissimus Græcorum, qui in expeditione
Troiæ fuerunt. Hic insaniam simulans comitatum negat, nem-
pe irretitus amore iuvenculæ coniugis Penelopes: verùm frau-
de à Palamede detecta, cogitur cum cæteris in bellum profici-
sci. Detectus ipse, Achillem vicissim detegit, qui etiam in Tro-
ianos contendit, anno mundi 2773.ante Christum natum 1189.
Ulysses multa tum fraude tum virtute peregit annis decem in
obsidione Troiæ: qua capta, per decennium itidem hac atque
illac fluctibus marinis iactatus, tandem ad uxorem in patriam
pervenit: procorum iniurias ulciscitur. Postea à Telegono,
quem ex Circe susceperat, spina trigonis piscis venenata, inco-
gnitus transfigitur. Homer. in Odyss. & Vergil.in Æne. multis
in locis.
PENELOPE, Icarij & Peribœæ filia, Ulyssis uxor fuit ca-
stissima. Hæc totos viginti annos maritum illibata pudicitia
expectavit, nec unquam adduci potuit ut alteri nuberet: quan-
quam pater Icarius cogeret, & proci valde solicitarent, quos
egregio commento fefellit (si credere licet) quanquam aliter
de huius pudicitia scribat Lycophron. Vide Ovid. epist. Heroi-
dum prima, quæ nomine Penelopes inscribitur.

page.notes: The woodcut ornament below the text is not transcribed. The medallion legends are read from the scan; the right medallion's second word ("VLY.CON.") is doubtful. Some printed spacing is irregular ("2773.ante", "Vergil.in"), left as printed.

page.layout: Two medallion portraits with legends at the top, centred above the text; one column of running text below them, with two entries and a printer's ornament at the foot. No margin notes.

main_text.l: ACHILES.
POLYCENA. F. PRI.
ACHILLES Pelei Thessaliæ regis & Thetidis filius, Gr-
æcorum fortissimus fuit. Hic iam adultus inter Lycomedis filias,
muliebri indutus ornatu latitauit, opera matris quæ hac arte
cavebat ne ad bellum Troianum proficisceretur, unde nō esset
reversurus. Nihilominus tamen Ulyssis astu deprehensus, ad
bellum perducitur. Hic Deïdamiam Lycomedis filiam com-
pressit, ex qua Pyrrhum sustulit: quinetiam ob ereptam sibi ab
Agamemnone Briseïda, pugnare destitit, donec Patrocli ami-
cissimi mors nunciaretur, quam Hectoris morte compensauit.
Cæterùm à Paride tum demum interficitur Achilles: tandem
& ipse Pyrrhus Polyxenam ad sepulchrum patris immolat. Ho-
mer.in Odyss. & Vergil.lib. Eneid.2. & Statius libr. Thebaid.1.
item Dares, & Dictys Cretensis.
POLYXENA Priami & Hecubæ filia speciosissima, ad
tumulum Achillis à Pyrrho eiusdem Achillis filio, interficitur,
ad placandos Achillis manes. Ouidius lib.13. Metamor.

l.i: Placet Achilleos mactata Polyxena manes.

main_text.l: Polyxenam fertur Achilles in mœnibus Troiæ conspectam ad-
amasse, eámque in uxorem petiuisse: Priamus annuit: in Apol-
linis templum conuenitur, ad ineunda pacis nuptiarúmque
fœdera: verum inibi interim Achilles à Paride dolo interfici-
tur. Vide ut supra, & Euripi. Trage.

page.notes: Two woodcut medallion portraits (Achilles in helmet; Polyxena with diadem) with legends as transcribed. Printer's ornament at the foot of the page, not text, not transcribed. Stains and show-through left out. No doubtful readings.

page.layout: Two medallion portraits with inscriptions at the top, centred; below them one column of running text, full width; the text ends with a catchword-free signature line at the bottom right. No margin notes, no footnotes.

main_text.l: NAVPLIVS
EVBOEAE REX
PALAMEDES
NAVPLIVS, Euboëæ insulæ Rex, quam Nigropontum
hodie vocant, Palamedis pater fuit, eius inquam qui Vlyssis
commento & fraude, ab exercitu lapidibus est obrutus: Vlysses
siquidem oderat Palamedem, mortemque illi dolo machina-
tus est, quòd technam suam detexisset, cùm illi furorem simu-
lanti, vt ad bellum minimè proficisceretur, filium in sulco ob-
iecit. Nauplius vt filij necem vlciscereretur, vxores principum
Græcorum, tum cùm Troiam obsidebant, in iuuenum adulte-
ria pellexit, sperans vt in reditu mutuis se vulneribus confode-
rent propter vitiatas vxores. Præterea Græcis redeuntibus,
ignem ex Caphareo monte ostendit: quò factum est vt bona
pars ad ignem, tanquam ad proximum portum adnauigans, in-
ter scopulos naufragium fecerit. tandem doloris impatientia
se ipsum in mare præcipitat, quòd Vlysses & Diomedes, quos
maximè obrui cupiebat, incolumes euasissent. Vide Homer.
Verg. Ouid. multis in locis singulos.
PALAMEDES Nauplij filius, quatuor dicitur literas
inuenisse, præterea ordinem aciei, symbolum bellicum, & vi-
gilias, ad exemplum gruum: item calculorum ludum, atque
aleam, & latrunculos, quos scachos vulgò dicimus, & mensu-
rarum ac ponderum rationem, quinetiam annum ad Solis cur-
sum, menses ad Lunæ accommodasse. Hic ab Vlysse falsò pro-
ditionis insimulatus, lapidibus obruitur. Vide Ouid. lib. 13. Me-
tamor. Cel. Rhodig. lib. 20. cap. 27. & lib. 7. ca. 31. Huius Palame-
dis Poemata dicitur Homerus, inuidiæ stimulis agitatus, con-
cerpsisse, aut exussisse[?]. idem Cel. Rhodig. id tradit, lib. 20. ca. 30.
Vide item Volat. lib. 18. & Plin. 7. cap. 56.

page.notes: The two medallion inscriptions are set in the engraving and are transcribed as lines above the text. "exussisse" is read from a worn word and is marked [?]. Long s is printed as s throughout and is rendered as plain s.

page.layout: Top: running head at upper right, page number at upper left. Below them two circular medallion portraits side by side, each with a vertical inscription (left "IEPTB", right "ABZAN"). Below the medallions one column of running text in two paragraphs. A small woodcut ornament at the foot, without text.

main_text.l: IEPTB[?]
ABZAN
IEPHTE, filius Galaad ex meretrice, iudicauit populum
Israël anno mundi 2787. ante Christum natum 1175. Hic pu-
gnauit contra Ammonitas, quos tradidit dominus in manus
eius. vouerat autem prius, satis tamen imprudenter, se in holo-
caustum oblaturū domino eum qui primus de domo sua egre-
diens, sibi occurreret victori: accidítque vt filia sua vnigenita
cum tympanis & choris ei reuertenti occurreret, qua visa sci-
dit ipse sua sibi vestimēta, præ dolore: immolauit tamen filiam
post duos menses, quos illa impetrarat ad lugendam virginita-
tem. Vide lib.Iudi.cap.11.& 12.sex annis iudicauit Iephte Israë-
lem. Ioseph.lib.Antiq.5.cap.12.
ABESAN, de Beth-lehem, mortuo Iephte iudicauit Is-
raël septem annis. Hic habuit triginta filios & totidem filias,
quas omnes maritis tradidit, simul filiis omnibus vxores dedit:
foras misit filias, filiorum autem vxores domum suam intro-
duxit. Iudi.12. Ioseph.lib.5.cap.12. Rabbi Salomon & Chaldæus
paraphrastes hūc Abesan Boos esse dicunt. Post Abesan, Aelon
de tribu Zabulon, iudicauit populum annos decem: post quem
etiam Abdon de tribu Ephraim, iudicauit Israëlē annos octo.
Iudicum cap.12. post hunc Samson iudicauit, cuius meminero
postea.

page.notes: Medallion inscriptions are set vertically along the rims; the first letter of the left one is read as B, possibly E, so marked [?]. Woodcut portraits and the ornament carry no further text. Greek and Hebrew: none printed. Marked "Vide lib.Iudi.cap.11.& 12." kept as printed (the reference "fex" is printed as such, probably "sex").

page.layout: Top: two engraved coin medallions side by side, with their legends (not transcribed as text). Below them: one column of running text, two paragraphs. Under the text, right: gathering signature. At the bottom: a printer's ornament. Running head at top centre, page number at top right.

main_text.l: LATINUS Laurentum Rex,Fauni & Maricæ, filius fuit.
Hic vel bello ab Ænea victus, vel tantùm certior factus quís-
nam,& unde esset Æneas,antequam signa canerent,ipsi Ænea
dextram,fidei signum,dedit:filiam deinde in uxorem tradidit,
quanquam prius pacta esset Turno Rutulorum regi.Æneas de
nomine uxoris Lauiniæ, Lauinium appellat. Turnus ob præ-re-
ptam Lauiniam sibi pactam , bellum mouet: utrinque summa
contentione pugnatum est: inclinauit tamen victoria in Tro-
ianos , qui Latinum eo in prælio amisere, anno mundi 2787.
ante Christum natum 1175. Titus Liuius lib.1. & Diony. Ha-
licar.lib. item primo.
LAVINIA Latini & Amatæ filia, Æneæ uxor post Creu-
sam fuit. Hæc mortuo Ænea Ascanij tutelam gessit: deinde ab
eodem Ascanio, Lauinio, urbe iam florente atque opulenta,
donata est:nouā.ipse[?] aliam sub Albano monte condidit, quam
ab situ porrectæ in dorso urbis, Longam Albam appellauit.
Titus Liuius lib.1. Lauinia Syluium Posthumum peperit ter-
tium regem Latinorum: qui sic dictus est,quòd post patris Æ-
neæ fatum in syluis natus ac educatus sit. Videto ut supra.

page.notes: Two engraved coin medallions above the text, not transcribed as printed text. Left coin legend: LATINVS (curved, left side) and AMATA (right side), showing two profile heads. Right coin legend: LAVINIA, showing a female profile head. Printer's ornament (decorative cartouche with a mask) below the text, not transcribed. "nouā.ipse": the a carries a macron, read with uncertainty. Spelling u/v changed per rules in running text: uxor, unde, utrinque, ut, urbe, urbis; capitals LATINUS (vowel U). The paragraph beginning "LAVINIA" opens with a capitalised name in other type, so it is kept as a paragraph, not a heading.

page.layout: Top: two circular medallion portraits side by side, each with its legend in capitals (AENEAS TROIANVS; TVRNVS). Below them one column of running text, full width. No margin notes, no footnotes.

main_text.l: AENEAS TROIANVS
TVRNVS
ÆNEAS, Anchisæ & Veneris filius, ac Priami gener, pius,
probus ac bellicosus à Vergilio in gratiam Augusti describitur:
aliter enim scribunt grauissimi autores. Hic patrem humeris
impositum Troiano incendio dicitur eripuisse, Creusam uxo-
rem in turba amisisse, in Italiam navigasse, Turnum bello vi-
cisse, Lavîniam duxisse, oppidum condidisse Lavinium, de no-
mine uxoris sic dictum: Ascanium, qui Albam Longam condi-
dit, genuisse. Aduentum autem Æneæ in Africam, cögressum,
societatem aut nuptias cum Didone, ut fabulosa praetereo: ne-
que enim appulisse in Africam scribunt historici probatiores:
neque, ut appulerit, Didonem illic potuerit reperisse, cum non-
dum nata esset. Nauigationem Æneæ sic paucis describit Ti-
tus Liuius lib.1. Aeneas, inquit, domo profugus, primo in Macedo-

l.i: niam venit: inde in Siciliam, quaerens sedes, delatus est. Ab Sicilia, classe

main_text.l: Laurentem agrum tenuit. Troia & huic loco nomen est. De morte
Æneæ nil certi reperi. Constat dum cum Rutulis ac Hetruscis,
congreditur, multos utrinque caesos, Aeneæ autem corpus nus-
quam inuentum. id praelium commissum est postquam treis
annos ab obitu Latini soceri sui, regnasset Æneas, anno à capta
Troia septimo. Dion. Halicar. lib.1. Titus Liuius lib.1. Verg. in li-
bris Aeneidos. Lavinium vrbem condidit Aeneas anno mun-
di 2788. ante Christum natum 1174.
TVRNVS, Rutulorum Rex, Amatæ, uxoris Latini, con-
sobrinus fuit. Huic pacta fuerat Lavinia ante aduentum Ae-
neæ: quare praelatum sibi aduenam ægrè ferens, simul Aneæ
Latinóque bellum intulit. Vide ut supra. Victus singulari cer-
tamine Turnus ab Aenea, victoriam cum sponsa, rivali Aneæ
reliquit. Verg. lib. Eneid. 12.

page.notes: Medallion legends transcribed as printed (AENEAS TROIANVS; TVRNVS). Two Latin words in the text are printed with spacing or accent marks that may not be exact: "Lavîniam" (first occurrence, possibly misread accent; printed as Lauiniam) and "Latinóque" (acute accent as printed). Long s rendered as plain s throughout. The printed u/v forms were normalised to modern u/v usage per the rules. Printed hyphens kept at line ends: "uxo-rem", "vi-cisse", "condi-dit", "Macedo-niam".

page.layout: Two engraved medallions side by side at the top, each with a portrait and a legend; below them one column of running text; no margin notes; signature at the foot right; running head and page number at the top.

main_text.l: ORESTES occiso Ægistho imperat Mycoenis, quæ urbs
est in Peloponneso, anno mundi 2789. ante Christum natum
1173. Fuit hic Agamemnonis & Clytemnestræ filius: matrem
adulteram cum adultero suo Ægistho interemit, quòd patrem
suum etiam interemerat. Deinde Pyrrhum quoque interfecit,
quòd Hermionem sibi prius desponsatam, quæ & Pyrrhum
oderat, rapuisset, víque eam in uxorem sibi retinuisset. Ob hæc
scelera furiis agitatus vagabatur: habuit interim Pyladem fi-
dum itineris comitem ac periculorum socium. Pervenit itaque
Orestes in regionem Tauricam, ubi inventa sorore Electra,
cum ea, jam furore purgatus, migravit in Italiam. Orestes pro
Pylade, Pylades pro Oreste, uterque pro altero mori minimè
recusavit: sicut nec Nysus pro Eurialo, nec Eurialus pro Nyso,
uti est apud Verg. quare numeratur inter insigniora amicorum
paria. Vide Sophocl. in Electra, Euripid. in Oreste, Cicer. de ami-
citia, & lib. 2. de finib. Ovid. Epist. 8. Heroidum.
HERMIONE Menelaï & Helenæ filia fuit. Hæc à Tyn-
daro avo materno primùm pacta est in uxorem Oresti, interea
dum pater in bello Troiano militaret: qui etiam eandem Pyr-
rho, mortuo patre Achille, promittit. Pyrrhus reversus eam
rapit, ac retinet invitam: quamobrem indignatus Orestes Pyr-
rhum in templo Apollinis, ope Macarei sacerdotis interficit,
uxorémque suam Hermionem recipit. Videto Vergil. libr. 3.
Aeneid. Ovid. epist. 8. supradicta, quæ inscribitur, Hermione
Oresti.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions (roundels) at the top of the page, not text. Left: a helmeted profile portrait labelled with a legend reading roughly "ORESTES AGA·MEMNONIS" (partly [?]). Right: a female profile portrait with a legend reading roughly "HERMIONE" and "MENELAI" (partly [?]). The legends are part of the engraving and are not transcribed as text. Line-end break "ami/citia" in "amicitia": no printed hyphen, so written whole. Numbers "2 7 8 9" and "1 1 7 3" are printed with wide letter spacing; copied as 2789 and 1173. Spelling u/v and i/j normalised as instructed (e.g. vxorem to uxorem, inuenta to inventa, Ouid. to Ovid.).

page.layout: Full-width area at top: two circular medallion portraits with inscriptions around their rims (left: TROI. ASCANIVS; right: SYLVIVS POS...). Below them, one column of running text, with no margin notes.

main_text.l: TROI. ASCANIVS
SYLVIVS POS[?]
ASCANIVS Æneæ filius, Latinorum Rex fuit, anno à
mundo condito 2789. ante Christum natum 1173. Hic à flu-
uio Phrygiæ Ascanius dictus est: prætereà Ilus, ab rege Troia-
norum Ilo: quinetiam Iulus, à prima barbæ Lanugine. Vergil. Æneid.I.

l.i: At puer Ascanius, cui nunc cognomen Iulo-
Additur, Ilus erat, dum res stetit Ilia regno.

main_text.l: Huic puero flammula quædam supra caput apparuit, quæ nec
vrebat, nec manibus extingui poterat: hinc sumptum omen est,
futurum vt aliquando imperaret: idem narrat de Seruio Tul-
lio Liuius lib.1. Cæterùm Ascanius cum 25. annos in Lauinio
regnasset, Longam Albam condidit, ac nouercæ, quæ antea re-
stituta fuerat (nam priuignum Ascanium metuens, in syluas se
receperat) Lauinium reliquit: regni hæredem fecit Posthu-
mum fratrem suum ex diuersa matre, cùm nondum esset Iulus
eius filius ad regendum idoneus per ætatem. Imperauit Asca-
nius 38.annis, cùm Lauinio, tum Longæ Albæ. Ab Iulo eius filio
Iuliorum familia orta est.Eutrop.auctus.
SYLVIVS Posthumus Æneæ ex Lauinia filius, regnum
Latinorum tenuit post Ascanium, anno mundi 2827. ante
Christum natum 1135. Imperauit apud Latinos annis 29. de
ratione nominis huius, dictum est supra in Lauinia. huius tem-
poribus agebat Homerus, vt autor est Cassiodor. Vide Diony.
Halicarn.& Eutro.lib.1.

page.notes: The coin legends are printed inside the two engravings; they are transcribed above as lines. The right legend is partly cut off at the rim, so its last letters are doubtful. Small ornamental marks appear before ASCANIVS and SYLVIVS; they are not text and are left out. The Ascanius verse is printed in italic with a long-s form; it is copied as printed.

page.layout: Two oval medallion engravings with portraits (Samson left, Dalida right) across the top; below them one column of running text in two paragraphs; the signature "Ee 5" at the foot right; no marginal notes.

main_text.l: SAMSON filius Manue de tribu Dan,iudicauit post Ab-
don, populum Ifraëliticum annos 20. quorum initium fuit an-
no mundi 2818. ante Christum natum 1144. Hic vir fortissi-
mus leonis catulum sæuum ac rugientem,qui ei occurrebat,in
frusta dilacerauit quasi hœdum, nihil omnino gladij habens
præ manibus.post aliquot dies inuenit in ore huius leonis exa-
men apum ac sauum mellis. Hic propter ablatam vxorem , se-
getes Philisthinorum excussit, ligatis facibus ad caudas tercen-
tum vulpium. Maxilla asini mille Philisthinorum interemit:
Israëlitas à seruitute eorum liberauit, quibus 40. annis seruie-
rant.in Gaza cùm circundaretur custodibus in porta vrbis stan-
tibus, ipse consurgens circiter medium noctis, apprehendit
ambas portæ fores cum postibus & sera, imposuitque humeris
suis,& portauit ad verticem montis. Vide Iudi.14.& 15.cap.
Iosph. Antiq. lib.5. cap.13. post Samsonem Heli fuit summus sa-
cerdos ac iudex populi per 40. annos, cui successit Samuel, de
quo postea mentionem faciemus.
DALIDA, siue Dalila ,meretrix fuit, quam amauit Sam-
son. Hæc argento à principibus Philisthinorum accepto corru-
pta,amasium Samsonem tonsum prodidit, qui ab hostibus ca-
ptus, erutis oculis in carcerem detrusus est. Postea inde voca-
tus est vt luderet coram eis,qui excæcato & ligato volebant il-
udere: at ille cùm venisset, & coram illis luderet, inuocato
Domino ait: Domine Deus meus memento mei, & redde mihi nunc
fortitudinem pristinam, vt vlciscar me de hostibus meis. Tunc appre-
hendit columnas ambas ambabus manibus,& cecidit domus,
quæ cadendo interfecit ad tria millia vtriusque sexus Philisthi-
norum,vnà cum ipso.Consulito lib.Iudi.cap.16.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions above the text, each showing a bust portrait in profile within a circle; the left one is labelled SANSON and the right one DALIDA, both in the engraving itself. The text is set in roman with italics for the prayer. Possible doubtful readings: "Iosph." (the printed abbreviation of Iosephus reads oddly), "Consulito" (printed "Confulito", read as Consulito with long s as s). The reference "Ee 5" is the gathering signature.

page.layout: Top: two medallions side by side, each with a portrait and a circular legend (left: BRVTVS; right: IGNOGNE and VX·BRVTI). Below them: one column of running text, two paragraphs. Ornament at the foot (not printed text, omitted).

main_text.l: BRVTVS
IGNOGNE
VX·BRVTI
BRVTVS Ascanij Æneæ filij ex Syluio nepos(quanquam
alij censeant Syluium Æneæ filium Posthumum fuisse ) fertur
proceros quosdam, atque immanes viros sede sua expulisse:
insulamque eam de suo nomine Britanniam cognominasse,
quæ prius vocabatur Albion, ab Albina quadam Syriæ regis
filia, quæ vna cum 32. sororibus, interfectis ab se viris, à patre
expulsa, in hæc loco appulerat. Post annos circiter 50. ab exci-
dio Troiæ, id est circa annum à mundo condito 2832. ante
Christum natum 1130. cœpit in ea insula,quam magnam Bri-
tanniam vocant, regnare Brutus iste, illicque fertur liberos
genuisse tres, qui totidem sibi regna constituerunt: Locrum à
quo Locria:Cambrum à quo Cambra, nunc Vuallia: & Alba-
nactum, à quo Albania,quæ Scotia postea dicta est.Locrus fra-
tribus superstes, solus Britannia potitus est: post quem Mad-
dan annos quadraginta regnauit. hæc Raphaël Volaterranus
in Geographia,lib.3. de populis ac regibus Britanniæ, quam
nunc Angliam vocant. Supputationem annorum potes etiam
colligere,ac deprehendere in Ascanio Æneę filio,de quo à no-
bis dictum est supra,paulò antè, tertia ab hinc pagina.
IGNOGNE Pandrasi Leo-græciæ Regis filia,huius Bru-
ti vxor fuit, ex qua tres, qui supradicti sunt, liberos sustulit.
Videto Supplementum Chroni.lib.4. Item Chronica Chroni-
corum.

page.notes: Medallion legends are set in a circle; their reading order and the letters of "VX·BRVTI" and "IGNOGNE" are read from the scan and may be uneven: "VX·BRVTI" is partly cut by the medallion edge, so the final letters are uncertain. Some numbers are set with spaces or old-style zeros in the print (for example "3 2.", "5 o.", "2 8 3 2.", "1 1 3 o."); they are given here as their values. The page ends with a printer's ornament at the foot, which is not text and is omitted.

page.layout: One page of text, with two round portrait medallions above the text (no transcribable text in them except the legends); running head at top centre with page number at top right. Main text in one column, two paragraphs of biography with headings for each poet. No margin notes; footnote-like references are inline.

main_text.l: HOMERVS Græcus Poëta percelebris, clarebat circiter
annum mundi 2838. ante natiuitatem Christi 1124. secun-
dum Cassiodorum. nam Cornelius Nepos in libris Chronico-
rum refert ad longè posteriorem ætatem, puta ad annum mun-
di 3051. ante Christum natum 911. ante Romam conditam
160. annos. Natum itaque Homerum, vt inquit Plutarchus,
belli Troiani tempore, eiusdémque spectatorem fuisse, qui-
dam scribunt, alij 100. annis post, alij 150. Mater ad Meletem
fluuium eum peperit, ob idque Melesigenes appellatus est: po-
stea cæcus factus, Homeri nomen accepit. Duo præcipua poë-
mata scripsit, Iliada & Odysseam. Ilias gesta Græcorum & Bar-
barorum propter Helenæ raptum, sed præcipuè Achillis præ-
clara facinora complectitur. Odyssea verò, Vlyssis ex Troiano
bello in patriam reditum. Scribunt eum obiisse præ ingenti
mœrore, cùm ænigma à piscatoribus propositum non posset
dissoluere: ipsum autem ænigma erat huiusmodi: Quæcunque
cepimus, reliquimus: quæ verò non cepimus, habemus. Vide Plutarc.
in vita Homeri.
HESIODVS Poëta, paulò præcessit Homerum, imò &
coætaneus eius, & sanguine illi iunctus fuisse perhibetur. Certè
Herodotus scribit Hesiodum atque Homerum 400. non am-
plius annis ipsum præcessisse: extitit autem Herodotus circiter
annum mundi 2520. & ante Christum natum 1442. erat He-
siodus ex Ascra, vico Bœotiæ, vnde & Ascræus dictus. Hic pri-
mus ac princeps omniū, de agricultura versibus scripsit, quem
imitatus est Verg. in Georgicis. Scribebat in Bœotia Helladis,
vt inquit Plin. lib 18. cap. 24. de eius morte misera, cúrque à Lo-
crensibus quibusdam adulescentibus sit occisus, vide Plutarc.
in conuiuio septem sapientum.

page.notes: Two round woodcut medallions above the text: left legend "P. POET." and "HOMERVS"; right legend "HESIODVS" and "POETA." Those legends are part of the illustration, not transcribed as text. Some headings above are set in roman body type, not capitals-only headings; they are marked level 3 because they open the poet entries, though they are in running text form. Printed numerals such as "2838" and "1124" are copied as printed. A few words are uncertain due to the scan: "fluuium" and "Melesigenes" look correct; "Bœotiæ" is clear. No words are marked [?] because the print is legible throughout. Note that the printed text uses "s" style long s in the source; it has been written as plain s.

page.layout: Two circular medallion portraits at the top, side by side, each with an inscription around its rim; below them one column of running text in two paragraphs. No margin notes. Running head at top; page number at top left.

main_text.l: SAMVEL SACERDOS
SAVL REX ISRAEL
SAMVEL, Elcanæ filius ex Anna, iudicauit populum
Israël post Heli, anno mundi 2878. ante Christum natum
1084. Hunc filium mater diu sterilis, precibus à Deo impetra-
uit, quem etiam Deo obtulit. Arcam Dei reducunt Philisthi-
ni, quam tempore Heli ceperant: iudicauit Samuel annos 11.
iuxta Hebræos, puta vsque ad Saul, primum regem. Senex fac-
tus Samuel, constituebat filios suos Ioëlem & Abiam iudices
in Israël, qui cùm non ambularent in viis Patris, sed declinaret
ad auaritiam & munera, peruertentes iudicium, maiores natu
Israël petierunt à Samuele regem, qui iudicaret more gentium
cæterarum. Itaque Saul à Samuele vngitur in regem, præcipi-
ente Domino. 1. lib. Reg. cap. 1. 2. & 3. ad 9. vsque cap. Ioseph. lib.
Antiq. 5. cap. 15. & sequen.
SAVL filius Cis, de tribu Ben-iamin, vnctus est in regem
primum Israëlitarum, eodem anno quo Samuel filios suos
constituerat iudices: nempe anno mundi 2889. ante Christum
natum 1073. Erat Saul altior vniuerso populo à capite ad hu-
meros, quem videns populus clamauit, Viuat Rex. Ammonitas
& Philisthæos vicit. At contra præceptum Dei, non expectato
Samuele, sacrificans, abiicitur à Deo: item contra præceptum
Dei victis Amalecitis, regem eorum Agag & prædam reserua-
uit: filiam suam Michol Dauidi in vxorem dedit. Tandem vi-
ctus à Philisthæis, ne viuus in manus eorum veniret, à quibus
occideretur, seipsum propriis manibus interfecit. Vide 1. libr.
Reg. à fronte ad calcem. hunc lib. sunt qui vocent 1. Samuelis.
imperauit Saul annis duobus. Iosep. lib. 6. cap. 4. & sequen.

page.notes: The two medallions are engravings: left, a bearded high priest in a headdress with a staff, inscribed SAMVEL SACERDOS; right, a bearded king in a turban, inscribed SAVL REX ISRAEL. Some letters on the medallion rims are worn. The second paragraph's "Ben-iamin" and "vi-ctus" are hyphenated at line ends as printed. The word "declinarét" shows a mark over the final vowel that I have not reproduced.

page.layout: Top: two circular woodcut medallion portraits side by side, David (left) and Solomon (right), each with inscription around its rim. Below them: one page of running text in two paragraphs, no margin notes. Running head at top, page number at top right.

main_text.l: DAVID REX
IVDA ET ISR
SALOMON
REX
ISRAEL
DAVID filius Iesse (Iesse vocabatur quoque Isaï) regnauit
super tribum Iuda in Hebron, anno mundi 2 8 9 r. ante Chri-
stum natum 1 0 7 1. quo tempore etiam Isboseth constituitur
Rex super Israelem, regnauit autem Dauid super Iudā & Ben-
iamin in Hebron septem annos, & sex menses: præterea super
alias decem tribus, & super totum Israelem annos 3 3. Hic cùm
gregem patris pasceret, leonē & vrsum apprehensō mento oc-
cidit: quare nec diffidit adfuturum sibi Dei auxilium aduersus
Goliath: igitur lapide funda iacto, gigantem interfecit. Prophe-
ta Nathan eum homicidij arguit. Præterea proposuit ei Deus
per Gad Prophetam tria pœnarum genera, quòd populum nu-
merasset: aut septem annorum famem, aut trium mensium per-
sequente hoste, fugam, aut trium dierum pestilentiā: vltimum
elegit, inquiēs melius esse vt in manus Domini inciderent. tunc
vsque adeo sæuiit pestis vt 7 0 0 0 0. virorum hac lue perirent,
ad ædificationem templi populū & Salomonē filium hortatus,
descriptionem ac necessaria ad ædificationem dedit. annos na-
tus 70. moritur, ac sepelitur in Beth-lehem. 2. lib. Reg. 11. cap. &
sequen. Ioseph. lib. Antiq. 6. cap. 10. & sequentibus.
SALOMON filius Dauid ex Beth-sabea, incipit impera-
re in Israël anno mundi 2 9 3 1. ante Christum natum 1 0 3 1. Hic
sapientiam à domino postulauit, & impetrauit. habuit ad ædifi-
cationem têpli 70000. qui onera portarent, latomorum 80000.
præpositorum 3300. locutus est 3000. parabolas, fuerunt carmi-
na eius 5000. annuus reditus eius erat 666. talentorum auri, ex-
cepto vectigali, valebátque talentum auri ad 5000. aureorum.
mira potes legere à cap. 4. li. 3. Reg. ad 10. item apud Iosep. lib. 8.
vxores habuit quasi reginas 700, & concubinas 300. quæ cùm
ex gentibus essent, vt eis gratificaretur, ad idololatriam defle-
xit: quare decem tribus à filio suo ablatæ. regnauit annos 40.

page.notes: Two woodcut medallion portraits at the top: David (left, crowned, with beard) and Solomon (right, crowned, with beard). Their inscriptions are transcribed above as lines. The inscription at the right of David's medallion is partly worn and reads as given. No marginal notes, catchword or signature on this page. Printed numerals in the text are set with spaces between digits, copied as printed.

page.layout: One page of text. Two coin woodcuts (medallions with portraits and legends) at the top, not text. Below them, one full-width column of running text. A decorative ornament at the foot, not text. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: ROBOAM filius Salomonis ex Naama Pharaonis filia,
mortuo patre regnavit super filios Israël qui habitabant in ci-
vitatibus Juda, anno mundi 2971.ante Christum natum 991.
nam decem tribus ad Jeroboam defecerant.Hic Roboam spre-
to senum consilio, juvenum consilium amplexatus est, super-
bissimè respondens populo qui tributorum imminutionem po-
stulabat:quamobrem desciuerunt ab eo decem tribus. ipse au-
tem 80000. virorum congregavit ex tribu Juda & Ben-jamin,
ut sub jugum ejus qui filius & hæres Salomonis erat,mitterent
has decem tribus quæ ad Jeroboam defecerant: sed ut ne pu-
gnaret prohibuit Dominus, dicens à se factū esse istud, quem-
admodum per Ahiam Prophetam prædixerat. Vide 3. Reg. 11.
12.13.14.cap.& 2.Paralipomen.10.11.12.cap. Josephlib. Antiquit.
8.cap.7. & 8.regnavit annos 17, cui successit filius, nomine A-
bia, sive Abiam.
SESACH rex Ægypti, ascendit in Jerusalem, & tulit the-
sauros domus Domini,& thesauros regios & universa diripuit,
anno quinto regni Roboam. habebat Sesac in exercitu 1200.
currus, equitum 60000. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: Coin legends are engraved in the medallions and are not running text. Left medallion: "ROBOM" along the left edge and "R. IVDA" along the right edge. Right medallion: "SESACH R." along the left edge and "AE" at the upper right [?]. Some words in the first paragraph are hard to read at this scan resolution, notably "Josephlib." and the digits "2971" and "80000"; the spacing around the numbers may differ from the print. "defecerant.Hic" lacks a printed space, which is kept as printed. The Latin spelling was changed only for u/v and i/j as the rules require; "Ægypti", "defciuerunt", "factū" and "Abiam" are unchanged.

page.layout: Top: running head centred, page number at top right. Below it, two circular portrait medallions side by side, each with its inscription around the rim. Below them, one column of text: two paragraphs, full width. Below the text, a printed ornament (tailpiece), not text. No margin notes.

main_text.l: PROPH.
AHIA SILON
R. ISRAEL.
HIEROBOAM
AHIAS Silonites, Propheta, prædixit ipsi Ieroboam de-
cem tribuum ad se defectionem : nam apprehendens pallium
suum nouum quo opertus erat ipsemet Ahias, scidit illud in
duodecim partes : & ait ad Ieroboam, Tolle tibi decē scissuras:
hæc enim dicit Dominus Deus Israël : Ego scindam regnum de
manu Salomonis, & dabo tibi decem tribus. Vide 3. lib. Reg. cap.11.
Ioseph.lib.Antiquit.8.cap.7.
IEROBOAM filius Nabat regnauit in Israël super de-
cem tribus, eodem anno quo Roboam imperauit duabus tri-
bubus, Iudæ scilicet ac Ben-iamin, nempe anno à mundo con-
dito 2971. ante Christum natum 991. Hic Ieroboā fecit duos
vitulos aureos ad retinendum populum ne ascenderet, ado-
randi gratia, in templum Ierosolymitanum, & ne hac forte via
deficeret ad regem Roboam, qui Ierosolymis imperabat. Sic
falsa religione propter ambitionem & regnandi libidinem, po-
pulum imbuit, nam adorandos hos vitulos palàm exhibuit, cla-
mans : Nolite vltrà ascendere in Ierusalem, ecce Dij tui Israel, qui te
eduxerunt de terra Aegypti. Hic manum in Prophetam extendit,
& aruit, nec potuit eam rex ad se retrahere: at verò orante Pro-
phèta, restituitur in integrum manus arida. Tandem à filio
Roboam, Regis Iudæ, vincitur. Rexit Israëlem annis 22. suc-
cessit Nadab filius eius. Vide 3.lib. Reg.cap.11.12.13.14. Ioseph.
lib. Antiq.8. cap.8.9.11.

page.notes: The two medallions are woodcut portraits with inscriptions around the rim (left: PROPH. / AHIA SILON; right: R. ISRAEL. / HIEROBOAM), transcribed above. The printed ornament below the text is a decorative tailpiece and is not transcribed. The "Ɲ" of "Nolite" is a decorative capital, transcribed as N.

page.layout: One page of text, two round medallion portraits at the top (no text block beside them); below them one full-width column of running text in two paragraphs. No margin notes. Running head at top centre; page number at top left.

main_text.l: ABIA, seu Abiam, filius fuit Roboam, ex Maacha filia A-
bessalom,& successit patri in regno Iudæ, anno mundi 2988.
ante Christum natum 974. Hic prauum se, ac paternorum ve-
stigiorum æmulum præstitit: orantibus tamen Deum suis mili-
tibus, vicit ipsum Ieroboam. tunc corruêre 50000. virorum
fortium ex Israël, confossi à viris Iuda. Nam diuisæ erant duo-
decim tribus Hebræorum in duo regna, Iudæorum, & Israëli-
tarum: præerâtque rex Iudæorum duabus tantùm tribubus, vi-
delicet tribui Iudæ,& Ben-iamin: Rex verò Israëlitarum impe-
ritabat reliquis decem tribubus. Rexit itaque Abia Israëlem
tribus ferè annis 3.Reg.15.cap.& 2.lib.Paralip.cap.13.Iosephlib.
Antiq.8.cap.11.
ASA, filius Abiæ, successit patri in regno Iudæ, anno 20.
regni Ieroboam regis Israël, imperauítque annos 41. Fuit Asa
rex pius in Deum & homines, subuertit altaria peregrini cul-
tus, confregit statuas, lucos succîdit: & præcepit Iudæ vt quærerêt Dominum Deum patrum suorum,legi diuinæ parëret,&
vniuersa mandata impleret. Habuit de tribu Iuda 300000.de
Beniamin autem 250000. militum virorum fortissimorum.
Egressus est contra eos Zara rex Ethiopum cum decies cente-
nis hominum millibus: hos implorato diuino auxilio, fugauit
Asa: fugatos,internecioni dedit. Post hæc iniit fœdus cum Be-
nadab rege Syriæ,timens Baasa regem Israël: quare à Propheta
Hanani corripitur, quem in neruum misit. Deinde dolore pe-
dum grauissimo laborans, cùm iam multos occidisset, opem
medicorum potius quàm Dei quæsiuit. 3.Reg.15.cap.2. Paralip.
14.& 15.Iosep.lib.8.cap.12.

page.notes: Two round medallion portraits with Latin inscriptions: left "ABIAS REX IVD", right "ASA REX IVD" (partly reversed/cut in the scan; read as "ABIAS R..." and "...SA REX ...UD"). Printed text is copied as it stands; "Iosephlib." and "Iosep.lib." are printed without stops as shown. Marginal marks: small circle and dot below the last line are not text and are omitted. The catchword and signature are absent.

page.layout: Running head centred at top ("PARS PRIMA.") with page number 65 at top right. Below it, two round portrait medallions side by side, each with its inscription around the edge. Below them, one full-width text block of two paragraphs, justified, with the first paragraph starting at the top. At the lower right, the gathering signature "Ff". main_text.l: ISRA NADAB R.
R. ISRAEL. BAASA
NADAB filius Ieroboam successit patri in regno Israël,
anno secundo regni Asa, Regis Iuda: hic impius, genuina pa-
tris proles, non diu imperauit: occisus est à Baasa anno tertio
Asa Regis Iudæ:& regnum eius occupauit homicida ille Baasa.
Vide tertium librū Regum,cap.14. & 15.imperauit anno à con-
dito mundo 2992. ante Christum natum 970.
BAASA occiso Nadab,regnauit super Israëlem annos 24.
homicidio regnum assecutus, homicidia iterum perpetrauit:
nam omnem familiam Ieroboam interfecit. fuit huic bellum
cum Asa, nam ascenderat Baasa in Iudam, & Rama muro cin-
gebat, vt ne quis à regno Iudæ in regnum Israël penetrare pos-
set: quamobrem perterrefactus Asa, missis muneribus opem
Ben-adab Regis Syriæ implorauit: vti dictum iam à me supra
est in Asa. Tandem Iehu prædixit ipsi Baasæ sui ipsius suorum-
que ruinam ob idololatriam, sicuti familiæ Ieroboam. successit
Baasæ Ela filius. incepit regnare Baasa anno mundi 2992. ante
Christum natum 970. nempe eodem anno de quo supra in
Nadab. Vide lib.3.Reg.15.& 16.cap.Iosephlib.Antiq.8.cap.12.

page.notes: The medallion inscriptions are read from the woodcut: left "ISRA" and "NADAB R." (the "ISRA" end is cut off by the edge, possibly ISRAEL), right "R. ISRAEL." and "BAASA". The reference "Iosephlib.Antiq.8.cap.12." has no clear space after "Ioseph" in the scan; it may read "Ioseph. lib." Possible printing error: "Iosephlib" is written without a space. The ornament at the bottom centre is a woodcut tailpiece with no text.

page.layout: One printed page. Top: running head "PROMPTV. ICONVM" and page number 66. Below: two round medallion portraits side by side, each with its legend around the edge. Below them: one column of running text in two paragraphs. A small woodcut ornament sits at the foot of the text.

main_text.l: ISRAEL
ELA R.
R. ISRAEL
AMRI
ELA filius Baasæ, defuncto patre imperat Israëlitis anno
mundi 3015. ante Christum natum 947.nempe anno 26. Asæ
Regis Iudæ: & anno 27. eiusdem ebrius occiditur à Zambri,
duce mediæ partis equitum huius Regis Elæ. Itaque Zambri
regnum inuadens occidit omnem familiam Baasæ: quod cùm
resciuit populus, constituit sibi alterū Regem nomine Ambri,
qui obsedit Zambri in Thersa. Porrò cùm videret Zambri ex-
pugnandam esse ciuitatem, ingressus palatiū succendit se cum
domo regia: sic tyrannide regnum assecutus, septimo etiam die
tyrannidem in semetipsum exercuit. Vide lib.3.Reg.cap.16.
AMRI (Iosephus Amarin vocat) Israëliticum regnum
administrauit anno mundi 3016. ante Christum natum 946.
nec verò nesciendum est, post Zambri diuisum fuisse populum
in duas partes, altera fauebat Thebni, altera Amri: hæc conten-
tio durauit ad aliquot annos: tandem præualuit pars quæ ele-
gerat Amri in Regem, & mortuus est Thebni: sic confirmatum
est regnum ipsi Amri, cuius regno etiam adduntur anni huius
dissentionis: nam dicitur imperasse in Israël annos duodecim.
Hic montem Samariæ emit à Somer (Samarû vocat Iosephus,
à quo Samaria dicta) duobus talentis argenti: illic ædificauit
Samariam, regniqué sedem constituit, sex annis in Thersa egit
reliquos in Samaria. Vide lib.3.Reg.cap.16. & Iosep.lib.Antiq.8.
cap.12. Successit ei filius etiam impius Achab.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are printed in the illustrations; the right one may begin with "R." before ISRAEL, which I read as [?] and copied as "R. ISRAEL". The ornament at the foot is decorative and not transcribed. No marginal notes are printed on this page.

page.layout: Running head at top centre. Two medallion woodcut portraits with inscriptions, side by side, above the text. One column of running text in two paragraphs below them. Signature "Ff 2" at the foot, right of centre. Page number at top right.

main_text.l: R. ISRAEL
ACHAB
JEZAB[?]EL REGIN[?]
ACHAB regnauit in Israel anno 38.regni Asa Regis
Judæ: hic erat annus mundi 3027.ante Christum natum 935. tenuit
Achab principatum in Samaria annis 22. omnes priores Reges
impietate superauit: duxit vxorem Jezabel Regis Sidoniorum
filiam: & posuit aram Baal in templo Baal, quod extruxerat in
Samaria, ipsumque Baal adorauit. Prædixit ei Propheta Elias
famem, quæ tres annos durauit. posthæc occurrit Achab Eliæ,
cui dixit: Tune es ille qui conturbas Israel? respondit Elias: Non ego

l.i: turbaui Israel, sed tu, & domus patris tui, qui dereliquistis mandata Do-

main_text.l: mini, & secuti estis Baal. Deinde miraculo facto in holocausto
Eliæ, eiusdem Eliæ jussu sacerdotes Baal impostores interfi-
ciuntur, erant autem 450. Achab semel atque iterum prælio
vicit Ben-adab: tertiò contra eundem pugnans mutata etiam
veste, sagitta fortuito ad mortem vulneratur. 3.Reg.16.cap.& seq.
Josep.lib.Antiq.8.cap.12.&13.
JEZABEL filia Eth-Baal Regis Sidoniorum, vxor fuit hu-
ius supradicti Acab. Impia hæc Pseudoprophetis Baal fauens,
Eliæ mortem minitata est: quod cùm resciret Elias, aufugit:
præterea ipsi Naboth mortem machinata est, qui lapidibus est
obrutus, quòd falsis testibus convicisset ipsa Jezabel, eum Deo
ac Regi maledixisse. occasio autem inde manarat, quòd vineam,
patrum suorum hæreditatem, Regi Achab non permisisset Na-
both. Vide lib.3.Reg.19. & 21.cap.& Josephus lib. Antiq.8. cap.13.
Hæc jussu Jehu de fenestra præcipitata est, in Jezrahel: cùm, au-
diens adventum eius, ornasset se, ac fuco faciem deliniuisset:
a spersúsque[?] est sanguine paries, & equorum vngulæ conculca-
verunt eam: jussitque eam sepeliri Jehu, quòd filia Regis esset:
at cùm sepelirent eam, non invenerunt nisi calvariam, & pedes,
& summas manus, juxta prædictionem Eliæ, 4.Reg.9.

page.notes: Two woodcut medallion portraits at the top: left, a bearded man in profile (Achab, king of Israel); right, a woman in profile wearing a crown (Jezabel, queen). The inscriptions around the medallions are partly cut off by the frame; the right-hand medallion's left-side inscription reads only "EL REGIN" and is reconstructed as [?].
