main_text.l: ANDRONICVS, ex tribus maribus, filiis Michaëlis
Paleologi, natu maximus, patri in imperio Constantinopolita-
no succedit, anno mundi 5255. à Christo nato 1293. Androni-
cus Michaëlem quendam, matre natum Hungarica, generum
ac imperij cõsortem assumpsit: quo mox defuncto, Andronicũ
Constantinum Despotem iuniorem, ad imperij successionem
inuitat: id Michaëlis prædicti filius Andronicus, moleste ferês,
in auum insurgit, Genuësium ope fretus, ius omne ad se trahit.
At Veneti seniorem cum restituissent Andronicum, tandem
prægrauantibus Bulgaris & Genuensibus, Venetos destituit,
partésque Ligusticas, à nepote coactus, amplectitur: & septua-
genario maior tandem moritur, anno postquam imperare coe-
perat decimo octauo. Vide Egna.lib.2.Cosmo.Munst.lib.4.
ANDRONICVS iunior, Michaëlis filius ex superioris
Andronici filia, sex & amplius annis cum Andronico auo præ-
dicto, varium ac anceps bellum gessit, sæpe tamen reconcilia-
tis animis, amicorum opera, & gratia malè sarta non coëunte.
Byzantium tandem clam ingressus, in auum nil molitur: quin
illum quoad vixit, secum imperare permisit: quo mortuo, cùm
aduersus hostes fortem se præstitisset, quinquagenarius obiit,
febre capitisque dolore intra quatriduum confectus, anno im-
perij circiter 16. coepit imperare anno mundi 5273. à Christo
nato 1311. Vide ut supra, & Chron. Phry. De hoc Andronico,
sequentibusque Imperatoribus ad Constantinum vsque, qui à
Mahomete, capto Byzantio, est obtruncatus, quot annis impe-
rarint, ac quo anno definito singuli coeperint, nil certi statuunt
autores: ordine tamen vniuscuiusque imago, ac vita, descriptæ
sequuntur.

page.notes: Engraved medallions at the top, without printed text of the book: left medallion legend partly visible, "ANDRONIC..." and "MICHAEL..." (cut off at the edge of the cameo); right medallion legend "IVNIOR." and "ANDRONICVS". A small dash-like mark stands before "ANDRONICVS iunior" at the start of the second paragraph; it is likely a printer's ornament and is not transcribed. A faint mark at the bottom centre is a smudge, not text. No marginal notes on this page.

page.layout: Running head with page number at top right. Two circular coin medallions with legends at top, side by side. Below them one column of running text. Gathering signature at the foot right. No margin notes.

main_text.l: IMP. ALBERTVS I AVG.
IMP. HENRICHVS VII AVG.
ALBERTVS Rudolphi filius,& Auftrię Dux,vti dictum
est, deuicto, ac occiso Adolpho, imperat anno mundi 5260. à
Christo nato 1298. Noluit primò Bonifacius Papa ratum ha-
bere imperium Alberti: postea tamen vltro confirmauit in o-
dium Philippi Pulchri Gallorum Regis: quinetiam donatum
Albertü titulo regni Gallici, extimulauit eum aduersus eüdem
Franciæ Regem. At Philippus data filia in vxorem filio Alberti,
placauit Albertum. Porrò Albertus filium suum Bohemiæ Re-
gem cõstituit: Bauaros & Maguntinos hostilia fœdera incëtes,
ita domuit vt parêrent imperio. Tandem à Ioanne fratris filio
prope Renum interficitur, anno imperij 10. Consulito Aemyl.
lib.8. Egna. li. 3.
HENRICVS Lucelburgensis, mortuo Alberto Impera-
tor creatur anno mundi 5270. à Christo nato 1308. Hic Comi-
tem Vuirtembergensem ,quòd Imperatori parêre nollet, iu-
gúmq; detrectaret,fortunis omnibus exuit. Deinde in Italiam
penetrans , Longobardiam capit, & Mediolani ferrea insigni-
tur corona. inde Romam profectus, post diadema acceptum,,
ab Vrsinis expellitur. Tandem graui obsidione Florentiam pre-
mens, veneno in Eucharistia dato, opera Dominici cuiusdam,
è medio tollitur,anno imperij 5. Hic Ioàni filio suo Regis Bohe-
mici filiam vxorem dedit: éstque ac occasione princeps Lucel-
bulgensis Caroli quarti pater, Rex Bohemiæ factus. Vide Ae-
my, lib.8.Egna. lib.3.

page.notes: The two coin legends are printed around the medallions and are given as lines above the text. "Consulito" is printed with a long s ("Confulito") and is read here as Consulito. "li. 3." is printed with the spacing shown. No marginal notes on this page.

page.layout: Top: running head across the page, with the page number at the top left. Below it, two round medallion engravings side by side (left: Othomanus, right: Orchanes), with their legends. Below the engravings: one column of running text in two paragraphs, with no margin notes and no footnotes.

main_text.l: TURC.R. OTHOMANUS
ORCHANES TURC.R
OTHOMANNUS regnat apud Turcas anno mun-
di 5261. à Christo nato 1299. Hic primus in ea gente hoc
nomen tulit, à castello Galatiæ à se capto: primúsque veterem
gentis gloriam asserere ausus est: nam gens ea Ierosolymam
ceperat anno mundi 4970. à Christo nato 1008. Sed à Chri-
stianis Gothofredo Bolione duce victi, ac pugna non incruen-
ta, fusi, fugatíque ad Niceam Turcæ, nullum dehinc Ducem
cuius extet memoria præcipuum habuere, ad hunc usque
Othomannum, qui primus neglecta paucorum potentia, Mo-
narchiam inuasit, primúmque in Turcica historia inter Impe-
ratores locum tenet. Hic cùm esset obscuriore loco natus, at-
tamen ingenio felix,cautus,diligens,ambitiosus regna semper
meditabatur: cui etiam impense fauit fortuna: nam magnam
Bithyniæ partem, plurimáque loca munita Ponto adiacentia
subegit: sed egregias suas victorias maximè nobilitauit, expu-
gnata Siua, quæ olim Sebastia dicebatur. Regnat annos 28.
obiit affecta ætate anno primo Philippi Valesij Regis. Pau. Io-
uius,& Munst.in Cosm.
ORCHANES Othomanni supradicti filius, post pa-
trem imperat anno mundi 5289. à Christo nato 1327. Hic
noua dignitate auctus,nihil mutatus,nec patri absimilis, quin-
etiam militaris disciplinæ peritior, liberalitate, facilitate, &
dexteritate fauorem & multitudinem undique comparans,
rem à patre inchoatam industria, studio, & prudentia auxit,
Mysiam, Lycaoniam, Phrygiam & Cariam domuit: Prusiam
(quæ nunc Bursia) Regum olim Bithyniæ sedem vi cepit, ac-
cepto ibi graui vulnere, quo postea interiit, anno primo Io-
annis Francorum Regis. Regnat anno 22. Pau. Io. Christoph.
Recherius lib. 1[?].

page.notes: Medallion legends are engraved in the images; read as TVRC.R. OTHOMANVS and ORCHANES TVRC.R, transcribed with u/v normalised. "Ierosolymam" is printed with a capital I that looks like l; read as Ierosolymam. "lib. 1" at the end is small and partly unclear; the numeral may be I. Heading names OTHOMANNVS and ORCHANES are run-in capitals opening paragraphs, so they are kept as paragraph text. No catchword or signature is visible.

page.layout: Two medallion portraits side by side at the top, each with a circular legend; below them one column of running text in two paragraphs; no marginal notes; signature at lower right; running head and page number at top.

main_text.l: IMP. LUDOVICUS IIII.
IMP. CAROLUS IIII AUG.[?]
LUDOVICUS Bavariæ Dux, Rudolphi Imperatoris ex
filia nepos, & Fridericus Austriæ Dux, variantibus Electorum
suffragiis, ambo Imperatores eliguntur anno mundi 5276.
à Christo nato 1314. His varia fortuna sæpe congressis, tandem
anno 8. victor Ludouicus, capto Friderico rerum potitur: sed
cùm se Imperatorem citra Papæ assensum scriberet, excommu-
nicatur. nihilominus Mediolanum venit, ubi ferream accipit
coronam: deinde Romæ summo acceptus honore à Stephano
Columnio coronatur. Petrum Corbariensem in Pontificem
creat: & oppidis iuris Pontificij alios dedit præfectos, Pontifi-
cem æmulatus, qui & ipse Galliæ Cisalpinæ multos autoritate
sua Regulos præfecerat. Imperauit Ludouicus annos 33. sumen
do[?] initium imperij eius ab excessu, & fato venenato Henrici
Lucelburgensis. Aemyl.lib.8.Egna.lib.3.
CAROLUS quartus Bohemus, Ioannis Lucelburgensis
Bohemiæ Regis, de quo dictum est supra in Henrico, filius, post
Edoardum Anglum & Guntherum Cæsares electos, Cæsar
quoque designatur: ad hunc Carolum res devenit, altero sub-
inde post alterum vita functo. Romæ itaque coronam hac con-
ditione accepit, ut confestim Italia excederet. laudem meruit
ob Auream bullam, in qua multa quæ ad pacem publicam per-
tinent, complexus est. Rerum Bohemicarum imprimis studio-
sus fuit: Pragæ gymnasium publicum instituit. obiit anno impe-
rij 32. Venceslao filio prius Cæsare creato, promissa Electoribus
pecunia, vectigalíque imperij illis obligato. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: Medallion legends are printed in the illustrations; transcribed as lines. The second legend's last word, read as AVG, is doubtful and set as AUG.[?]. "fumen do" at the line break is hard to read and may be a split word (sumendo); marked [?]. "vectigalíque" carries an accent as printed. Page number and running head are as printed (head with u/v normalised). No catchword is visible.

page.layout: One page of text, single column, with two medallion engravings at the top (Dante and Can Grande della Scala). Below them, two paragraphs of running text. A decorative ornament sits at the foot, with no text. Running head at top centre; page number at top left.

main_text.l: DANTES Aligerus, Florentinus, cùm humanioribus tum
diuinis literis instructissimus, Philosophus ac Poëta, nulli suo
seculo secundus, pulsus patria, in Gallia aliquandiu maximè
Parisiis, posteà apud Arragonum Regem exulans, de sua cala-
mitate varia edidit opera. Tandem exul etiam apud Rauen-
nam obiit, Ludouico Bauaro Imperante, anno mundi 5283.
à Christo nato 1321. Videto Trithemium de Scriptoribus Eccle-
siasticis, & Supplementum Chronicorum lib.13.
CANIS Scaliger, à rebus gestis, cognomento Magnus, Ve-
ronæ urbis dominium sibi vendicans, rexit eam annos ferè 20.
quam etiam variis ac superbis ædificiis ornauit. Picenum &
Romandiolam omnem sua potius virtute ac liberali humani-
tate, quàm armis subegit. Princeps hic eloquens, comis, libera-
lis, oratoribus, historicis, poëtis, omnibus denique doctis fauēs,
Dantem Florentinum ad se accersiuit, & præmiis ac honoribus
eum donauit. Hic sine virili prole moriens, duobus nepotibus,
Alberto inquam & Mastino fratribus, urbis tantæ dominium
reliquit: obiit Veronæ, atque inibi maxima funeris pompa se-
pultus est, anno à mundo condito 5291. atque à Christo nato
1329. Videto Chronicorum Supplementum lib.13.

page.notes: Two medallion engravings above the text, not transcribed as text. Left medallion legend reads "DANTES." on the left and "FLO. POE." on the right. Right medallion legend reads "CANE. SCALA" in partly worn letters; the first word is uncertain (possibly CANIS). The ornament at the foot is decorative only. Date figures "5283", "1321", "5291", "1329" are set with spacing in print and are copied without spaces. Printed "posteà" and "apud" run together in the line; copied as separate words. Reading of "Verona" line-end and the "Parisiis" line is clear.

page.layout: Running head at top, with page number at top right. Below it, two round medallion portraits side by side with their inscriptions (no text block). Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs, with a gathering signature at the foot right.

main_text.l: FRAN. 18.
PHILIPPVS
F.REX 52
CAROL[?]VS
PHILIPPVS Longus Ludouici Hutini Francorum Re-
gis frater, successit ei in regno Franciæ anno mundi 5277. à
Christo nato 1315. Hic Longus dictus est ob corporis proceri-
tatem ac gracilitatem: id vnum mirum est, quòd neque ab ec-
clesia, neque à populo quæ petebat tributa & vectigalia impe-
trare potuerit. Puteos elephantiaci à Iudæis persuasi, veneno
infecerunt: quæ res occasionem vt pestis grassaretur præbuit:
sed vtrique miserè, dato supplicio, perierunt. Constituerat Rex
efficere vt vbique ponderis, mensuræ & pecuniæ rario eadem
esset: sed morte præuentus id præstare non potuit. obiit anno
regni, quod per Saliquam legem adeptus erat, quinto, nullis
confectis bellis: nam festa pax vndique ridebat. in æde D. Dio-
nysij conditus est. Vide Paulum Æmylium de rebus Francorum
lib.8. Gaguin.lib.7. & Carionem lib.3.
CAROLVS huius nominis quartus, cognominatus Pul-
cher, Philippi Longi frater, Nauarræ Rex, quemadmodum
& tres Francorum Reges superiores, succedit fratri in Franciæ
regno anno mundi 5282. à Christo nato 1320. Hic in scelera
seuerissimè animaduertit, iustitiæ & æquitatis cultor fuit. Aqui-
taniam ingressus, Regum hic primus Papæ decimas permisit,
vt quæstus particeps fieret. has autem colligebat Papa, vt bello
lacesseret Ludouicum Bauarum Imperatorem, quem hostem
scilicet ecclesiæ iudicauerat. Regnat annos septem: moritur ad
saltum Vicenarum, sepultus in æde D. Dionysij, relicta vxore
grauida. Vide autores quos supra.

page.notes: Medallion legends: the right legend's name is partly obscured, read as CAROL[?]VS. No marginal notes are printed on this page. The line-end break in "Aqui-taniam" shows no printed hyphen, so the word is written whole. Long s is normalised to s throughout, and the f-like letters in "feuerissimè", "fcelera" and "fcilicet" are read as long s.

page.layout: Running head at top, with page number 184 at left. Below it, two oval portrait medallions side by side, each with its caption printed around it (left: R. FRAN. 50 / PHILIPPVS; right: REX FRAN. 51. / IOANNES). Below them, one full-width column of text in two paragraphs. No margin notes.

main_text.l: R. FRAN. 50
PHILIPPVS
REX FRAN. 51.
IOANNES
PHILIPPVS Valesius trium superiorum Franciae Regum
patruelis, Carolo Pulchro succedens, regnat apud Francos anno
mundi 5289. à Christo nato 1327. Flandri à Gallis profligantur:
Casletum capitur, spoliatur, incenditur. Ad Ambianos Regum
Franci, Angli, Bohemi, & Balearici fit coëuentus, Anglus clien-
tem se Franci Regis profitetur. Sacra arma Valesius induit con-
tra fidei Christianae aduersarios. Petrus Cunerius frustra cona-
tur temporalem Episcopis auferre iurisdictionem. Incipit ma-
ximum bellum Anglicu. Iacobus Arteuilla plebeius multas in
Flandria excitat turbas contra Flandrensem Comitē, qui se in
Franciam recipit. Galli & Angli Regum acies in conspectu fere
sine conflictu veniunt. Anglus quando Francus praelio abstinet,
Flandriam repetit, vbi Arteuillae consilio, lilia & Regis Franciae
titulum adsumit: quae hucusq; sibi arrogat. Ad Crefciacum pu-
gnatur tandem à nostris infeliciter. Calitium Anglis deditur, à
quibus recuperari nunquam potuit. Trapezitę Lõgobardi & Itali
capti, pulsi, ac proscripti sunt ex Francia ob immanes vsuras.
Rex forte accipit, interfurio relicto. Humbertus Princeps vili
Delphinatum vendit, ea lege vt primus Regis filius Delphinus
vocaretur, & Delphinatum obineret: itaque Dominicanum
Humbertus profitetur. Initio regni immanes exactiones fuere,
ac primum ex sale vectigal institutum. Regnat annis 22.obit ad
Nogentum regium, sepultus ad D. Dionysium. Æmy. lib. 8. & 9.
IOANNES Philippi Valesij filius, patri in regno succedit
anno mundi 5311. à Christo nato 1349. Hic ab Anglo, capitur,
ad quartum lapidem ab vrbe Pictonum, ac post annos 4. libe-
ratur: nec multo post iterum in Angliam traiicit vt de suis obsi-
dibus liberandis transigat: at morbo ante reditum praeuentus,
Londini moritur anno regni 14. ad D. Diony. Carolus quintus
patris Ioannis cadauer transtulit. Æmy. lib. 9.

page.notes: The two medallion captions are printed inside the woodcut images and are transcribed as lines. Some letters in the medallion captions are small and worn; "50" and "51." are read as printed. Spelling in the text is as printed (e.g. "Crefciacum", "tranfigat"). The tilde over the o in "Lõgobardi" and the macron forms are read from a slightly blurred scan.

page.layout: One page of text. Above the text, two medallion engravings side by side (left: portrait of two men; right: portrait of a bust). Running head at the top centre, page number at the top right. Signature at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: IOANNES Palæologus,dictus etiam Calo-ioannes,patri
Andronico iuniori succedit,licet Ioannes Cantacuzenus,tutor
prudens,imperium administret Constantinopolitanum circa
annum mundi 5290. à Christo nato 1328. Tutor itaque Can-
tacuzenus,ac imperij consors Apocauci fraude (viri quidem
obscuri,sed solertis & callidi,ac inter principis amicos ob eius-
modi mores,præcipuæ dignationis) & Patriarchæ ambitione,
in exilium truditur. iniuriæ impatiens bellum quinquennale
aduersus Reginam & Ioannem Cantacuzenum Imperatorem,
Andronici filium gerit,Turcarum arma Europæ primus infert.
Huic tandem proditur Byzantium:quod cum occupasset,nulli
molestus fuit,imperij tantum consortem egit,filia in vxorem
Ioanni tradita. Inde in Genuenses,sociis Venetis & Arrago-
niis,varia fortuna bellum gerit Cantacuzenus:cui & statim ab
Ioanne Palæologo exule prædicto bellum indictum,Turcarum
in primis ope geritur,quibus etiam in Europa locum primum
inhabitandum tradidit. Cum autem improuisus Byzantium,
ex Tenedo soluens,ingressus esset Palæologus,tandem Canta-
cuzenus imperio relicto,monachum egit. Palæologus Mat-
thæum Cantacuzeni filium participe imperij agere volentem,
imperium deponere coëgit. & cum multa bella confecisset Pa-
læologus,moriens filio Manueli imperiu reliquit. Vide Egnat.
lib.2.& Cofm.Mun.lib.4.
MANVEL prædicti Ioannis Palæologi filius,post patrem
imperat Constantinopoli: septem mares filios hic reliquit,quo-
rum Ioannes natu maximus,morienti successit. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: Medallion engravings above the text carry legends: left medallion "IO. CAN." and "IOAN. PALAEOL."; right medallion "MANV" and "EL. II" (partly legible, read from the illustration, not transcribed into the text). Scan is slightly grey; "imperiu" and "Cofm" are read as printed and may be doubtful. The left-hand word "Arrago-" is read as printed and may be doubtful.

page.layout: Two woodcut medallion portraits centred at top; below them one column of running text with two paragraphs (the first a biography of Amurathes, the second a short entry on Solimanus); full width. Printed running head at top with page number at left.

main_text.l: AMVRATHES huius nominis primus, Orchanis filius,
mortuo patre, apud Turcas imperat anno mundi 5311. à Chri-
sto nato 1349. Is auitam paternámque felicitatem æmulatus
est: at vero in Caramanum auum maternum non minus infe-
stus quàm pater fuit, qui socerum occiso eius filio adolescente
non minima Ciliciæ parte exuerat. Cæterùm à Constantinopo-
litano Imperatore Ioanne Palæologo solicitatus Amurathes
12000. Turcarum ei in auxilium mittit: idque initium ac origo
ruinæ imperij Constantinopolitani fuit. Nam Europeis opibus
illectus Amurathes, opis denuo adferendæ simulatione, potiun-
dæ tamen Græciæ animo, Genuensium nauibus vsus Amura-
thes, Thurcarum 60000. in Græciam transportat: Hellespon-
tum ad Abydum superat: Callipolim cum aliis oppidis occu-
pat: in ipsum quoque Imperatorem inexpectato grauem impe-
tum facit. Postea Seruiam, Bulgariamque ingressus, Lazarum
Seruiæ, & Marcum Bulgariæ principes, cum paratissimis copiis
ei occurentes, ingenti cæde profligat, prius occupata Adriano-
poli: sed Lazaro cæso, mox à feruo in domini vindictam Amu-
rathes occiditur, anno regni 23. Vide Egna.lib.2. Pau.Io.& Chri-
stop.Richerium de rebus Turcarum lib.1.
SOLIMANVS Amurathis filius, patri in imperio suc-
cedens, confestim hæreditariæ dignitati eripitur, atque per in-
sidias occiditur à fratre æmulo Baiazete: quamobrem à non-
nullis inter Turcicos Imperatores minimè annumeratur. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: Two medallion portraits: left labelled "THES TVRC R." and "AMVRA"; right labelled "SOLIMANVS R." and "AMVRAT". Lower-left faint show-through only; not transcribed. Several words in the text are set in a slightly lighter or uneven inking and were read with care; "Amurathes" in the first paragraph and the numerals 5311, 12000, 60000 and 23 are copied as printed (the printed numerals in the original read "5 3 11", "1 2 0 0 0", "6 0 0 0 0" and "2 3"). Where the scan is faint the reading is uncertain but no [?] markers were required.

page.layout: Running head at top, with page number at top right. Two medallion portraits side by side, each with legend text around its rim (left: F.REX.49 and CAROLVS; right: IOHN CAROLVS 6 and FR). Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs, full width. No notes in the margins.

main_text.l: F.REX.49
CAROLVS
IOH[?] CAROLVS 6
FR
CAROLVS quintus, Ioannis Francorum Regis filius,
patri in regno succedit anno mundi 5325. à Christo nato 1363.
Hic sapiēs cognominatur ob morum probitatem, & egregiam
regni administrationem: literas,& literatos coluit: Bibliorum
libros syncerè transferri iussit: ius ex æquo vt diceretur in pri-
mis curauit, iudiciisq; frequenter adfuit.togatus omnino fuit,
nec arma vnquā induit:tantum loca Lutetiæ vicina peragrans,
longinqua & grauia negotia, & bella, per fratres ac præfectos
suos administrauit:per quos quicquid patri ab Anglis ablatum
erat,id omne ferè recuperauit.vt belli impensis sufficeret,vecti-
gal sali,ac promercali vino imposuit. Aduersus Anglos exerci-
tus quinque potentisimos habuit.Carolus quartus,Imperator
ac Venceslaus filius Cæsar, in Franciā veniunt, vt inter Anglos
& Francos pacem componant:sed re infecta redeunt ob Regi-
næ,ac Isabellæ filiæ interitum. Lex Regis in Senatu promulga-
tur,vt Regum Franciæ filij anno 14.inungantur,& coronentur.
Bastildæ fundaméta iaciuntur Lutetiæ,Regis sumptibus. obiit
an.regni 16.in castro pulchritudinis ad saltum Vicenarum: se-
pultus ad D.Dionysium.Turlupini, qui se paupertatis societa-
tem vocitabant,delentur.Æmyl.lib.9.
CAROLVS sextus,Caroli quinti filius,adhuc adolescēs,
in Regem Franciæ consecratur, anno mundi 5342. à Christo
nato 1380. Hic Rex tres tantùm Liliorum flores pro insigni Re-
gum Franciæ gestare instituit. huic pater duodeuicies 100000.
aureorum reliquit:initio tamē regni filij, magnæ fisci angustiæ
fuerunt:huius adolescentia & crebra gubernantium mutatio,
tantam vim pecuniæ dissiparat. Armeniæ Rex à Turcis pulsus
in Franciam venit. Africum bellum conficitur. Regnat an. 42.
ad D. Dionysium sepultus. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are read from the image; the letters of the right medallion's left edge ("IOH[?]") are partly hidden. The printed "vecti gal sali" appears split as shown. Printed spellings such as "componant", "potentisimos", "impofuit", "fundaméta" and "Æmyl.lib.9." are left as printed. No marginal notes or catchword.

page.layout: Top: two medallion portraits side by side, each with its legend around the rim. Below them: one column of running text in two paragraphs. Below the text: a woodcut ornamental frame, no text. Running head at top; page number at top left.

main_text.l: FRANCISCUS PETRAR.
IO. BOCCATI FLO. RHE.
FRANCISCUS Petrarca, natione Hetruscus, vir do-
ctissimus, Philosophus, Rhetor, & Poëta celeberrimus, literas
velut intermortuas quasi ab inferis revocauit:nec minus sancta
conversatione quàm scientia claruit, multa opera tam in lingua
Latina, quàm in sua vernacula conscripsit. Amore Christi &
Philosophiæ salutaris vitam solitariam elegit, in qua Philoso-
phando, orando & scribendo perseuerans, moritur in Eremi-
torio suo agri Patauini, sub Carolo Imperatore huius nominis
quarto, & Gregorio Papa huius nominis undecimo, anno à
mundo condito 5536.à Christo nato 1374. Videto Trithemium.
IOANNES Boccatius Florentinus itidem Poëta, Philo-
sophus, & Astronomus eruditissimus, multa præclara volumi-
na tum Latino, tum vulgari suo idiomate conscripsit. moritur
statim post Petrarcam. Videto etiam Trithemium.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are printed on the woodcut rim (left: FRANCISCVS PETRAR., right: IO. BOCCATI FLO. RHE.) and are transcribed above with v/u normalised. Long s read as plain s throughout. The woodcut ornament below the text carries no printed words. Page number read as 188; the first digit is slightly worn.

page.layout: Running head at top, with page number at top right. Below it, two engraved medallions side by side (portraits of Gian Galeazzo and Giovanni Maria Visconti, with legends; the legends are part of the engravings, not text). Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs, full width. No notes in the margins, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.l: IO. GALEATIVS Vicecomes, Galeatij Mariæ filius,
anno mundi 5333. à Christo nato 1371. postquam more pa-
trum suorum, annos 17. Mediolani imperauerat, à Ladislao
Cæsare, Dux Mediolani creatur. Ut autem à suis inciperet,
Barnaba patruo occiso, opes eius & imperium occupauit. Hinc
Veronam, Vicentiam, & Paduam subiugauit. ad Occidentem,
Vercellas, Albam, atque Astam subegit. ad meridiem debella-
uit Aquas, Alexandriam, Tortonam, Bubbium, Placentiam,
Parmam, Regium, Bononiam, Pisas, Massam, Senas, Grosse-
tum, atque Clusium. & reuertens Perusium, Assisium, No-
ceam, Ciuitatem, Bellonam cepit & Feltrum: &(ut velut cir-
culum absoluueret) Brixiam, Bergamum, Laudem, Cremo-
nam, atque Cremam, subegit. Lucenses in deditionem acce-
pit. tota ipsum Italia reformidauit. Ticini ædificauit arcem
superbam, ad quartum verò lapidem, septum admodum in-
gens, ad feras omnis generis asseruandas, cum cænobio ma-
gnifico extruxit. fuit pulcher, doctus, & eloquens: sed impri-
mis sagax. Tandem 55. ætatis anno, post 24. imperij obiit, re-
licta Valentina, Caroli Regis Franciæ postea uxore. Paul. Io-
uius, & Supplementum Chro.
IO. MARIA Vicecomes, adhuc paruulus, & sub ma-
terna custodia, anno Salutis 1402. felicissim. patri successit. Hic
cum adoleuisset, multos innocentes occidit, & non paucos ini-
micos canibus vivos devorandos tradidit. Piam matrem de-
trusit in carcerem, ibíque eam sæuissimè mori coegit. Verùm
mox quasi Deo vindice, nudatus amplissim. bonis paternis, à do-
mesticis, post decem annorum tyrannidem, in templo trucida-
tur. Paul. Iou. & Supplementum.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions at the top, showing profile portraits of Gian Galeazzo Visconti (left) and Giovanni Maria Visconti (right), with circular legends. The left legend reads roughly "IO. GALEATIVS" and "DVX MLI" and the right legend roughly "IOANNES" and "DVX MLI", but the letters are partly worn and only approximately read. Doubtful readings: "absoluueret" (the uu spelling is unclear), "felicissim." and "amplissim." (the abbreviation mark is uncertain, possibly meaning -issimè). A small stray slash mark appears centred below the second paragraph; it is not printed text and is not transcribed. Faint show-through of the reverse side is present and not transcribed.

page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre with page number at top left. Two medallion portraits side by side above the text. Main text in one column of two paragraphs below them, with no marginal notes.

main_text.l: BAIAZETES Turcarum Rex quartus, siue Pazaites,
huius nominis primus, mortuo patre Amurathe Solimanum
fratrem per insidias occidit, folúsq; imperio potitur anno mundi
5335. à Christo nato 1373. Hic Marcum Bulgariæ principem
prælio superatum trucidat, patris mortem vlturus: bonámque
Bulgariæ partem debellat: neque ita multò post, crudelissimas
in Hungaria, Albania, & Valachia excursiones fecit: Christia-
nos quamplurimos ligatos in Thraciam duxit. In negotiis exe-
quendis tanta vsus est celeritate, vt Baiazetes Hildrin, id est
cœli fulgur cognominaretur. Animi itaq; ac corporis doribus
adiutus totam ferè Græciâ subegit. Constantinopolim obsedit
annis 8. cuius Imperator in Galliam nauigat, auxilium implo-
raturus, quod & obtinet. Baiazetes autem Gallos, Hungaros,
Germanos ac Seruianos, siue Mysios, semel ac strenuè superat:
atque ad obsidionem Constantinopolitanam reuertitur: neque
vlla ratione imperij caput illud seruari poterat, ni Tamberla-
nes, Orientalis Scythiæ Rex, ei occurrisset, qui Baiazetem ad
Stellam montē, vbi cum Mithridate Pompeius pugnarat, vicit,
catenísq; aureis ligatum, atque in ferream caueam detrusum,
per totam Asiam ac Syriam circunduxit, donec etiam in fata
concederet. Vide Egna.lib.3.Pau.Iouium, de re.Turc.
TAMBERLANES Zagataiæ Orientalis Scythiæ re-
gionis, versus Parthiam ac Sogodianam princeps, peditum ac
equitum infinita pene multitudine fretus, Turcarum 200000.
vnico congressu cecidit, Regémque eorum Baiazetem, vti di-
ctum est, cepit, circa annum Domini 1397. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: Two medallion portraits above the text, labelled "TVRC.R.4." and "BAIAZETES" (Baiazet) and "TAMBERLANES" and "TAR.IMP." respectively. Not transcribed as text. The number "200000" in the second paragraph is printed with a trailing mark, read as 200000. Possible printing inconsistencies: "Hildrin" and "Stellam montē" kept as printed.

page.layout: One page of text. Running head at the top, with the page number at the top right. Below it, two coin engravings side by side. Below them, two paragraphs of running text in one column. A decorative ornament (fleuron) at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: VENCESLAVS succedit Carolo patri Imperatori hu-
ius nominis quarto, imperatq; post eum anno mundi 5340. à
Christo nato 1378. hic nec patri, nec avo similis fuit: cum pa-
tre tamen annos 8. regnarat: tandem solus ignauissimè rem ad-
ministrat annis 22. Cæterum à Sigismundo fratre captus est,
móxque Electores ei imperium abrogant, in cuius locum Ro-
bertum Bauarum sufficiunt. Porrò Galeatius Vicecomes Me-
diolanensis bonam Italiæ partem suo dominio adiicit, atque à
Venceslao, pro Vicecomite, Dux Mediolanensis dicitur. tunc
igitur in Ducatum erectus est primùm Vicecomitatus Medio-
lanensis. Apud fratrem in carcere apoplexia obiit Venceslaus.
Blond.lib.io.[?]deca.2.Egna.lib.3.
ROBERTVS, qui & Rupertus, Bauariæ Dux, deiecto
Venceslao, imperat anno mundi 5362. à Christo nato 1400.
Hic ut Florentinis gratum faceret, ad comprimendam Galeatij
potentiam, in Italiam traiicit: verùm cum eo ad Benacum con-
gressus, facilè repellitur: unde mox ad Venetos deflexit: & in-
cassum Florentinis adnitecibus[?] ne Italia exiret, in Germaniam
retro abiit, paci, religionique vacaturus, Florentinos interim in
magno relinquens discrimine. Obiit post annos ex quo impe-
rauit decem. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: Two engraved coin medallions at the top, not text. Left coin: laureate head facing left, legend "IMP. VENCESLAVS AVG." Right coin: head facing right with a crown or diadem, legend "IMP. RVPERTVS" with "P.F. AVG." on the left. The legends are copied as engraved. Doubtful readings: "io" in "Blond.lib.io" (perhaps 10) and "adnitecibus" are marked [?]. The printed "hu ius" is a line-end split of "huius" without a hyphen, and is written whole. Spelling of u/v and i/j is normalised as instructed (ut, unde, Vide); other spellings are as printed.

page.layout: Two medallion portraits (coins) at the top, side by side, with their printed legends; below them one column of running text, two paragraphs; no marginal notes; running head at the top, page number at the top left.

main_text.l: CYRISCELEBES, quem alij falsò Calapinum dicunt,
Baiazetis filius natu maximus, cū fratribus post patris cladem
fugiens, Asiáque à Tamberlane spoliatus, & ad Imperatorem
Constantinopolitanum pro singulari præda deductus, regiéq;
apud eum educatus, postea summa Imperatoris clementia solu-
tus est: in Asiámque discedens, paternum imperium recuperat.
Instauratis itaq; imperij viribus, aduentanti Sigismundo Hun-
gariæ Regi fortiter se opposuit, qui Salumbezenes campos oc-
cuparat, sperans vires non resumpturos Turcas post tantam à
Tamberlane acceptam cladem: sed non magis sibi fauente for-
tuna quàm, cùm ad Nicopolim pugnas cum Baiazete, fauerat,
fugere cogitur Sigismundus: cuius pedites ante sagittis cōfossi
sunt, quàm in phalangē dispositi cominus congredi cùm hoste
potuerint: equites verò ad primum statim aduentantis hostis
impetum terga verterunt. Victor Cyriscelebes cum Despotam
bello lacessere inciperet, morbo præventus in ipso ætatis flore
obiit anno regni 6. Pau.Iouius de rebus Turcicis.
ORCHANES patri Cyriscelebæ, tenella adhuc ætate
adolescentulus, ac unicus imperij hæres, ad imperium cùm co-
naretur paucorum studio atque opera admitti, à Mose patruo
interficitur. Moses statim dignum illo parricidio exitium tulit,
à fratre Ma-hometé vita bonísque priuatus. Sunt qui hunc Ma-
hometem, nulla prorsus facta de Cyriscelebe, Orchane, & Mo-
se mentione, à morte Baiazetis statim imperasse tradant: quare
nullam hîc supputationis annorum rationem habuimus, sicuti
nec Chronici. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: Coin legends printed inside the engravings, not running text: left coin, reading round the edge, "TVRR" (partly obscured) and "CYRISCELEBES"; right coin, "CIRIS.F" and "ORCHANES". The left legend's first letters are doubtful. Doubtful readings: "Ma-hometé" (accent uncertain), "Turcas", "Asiáque" and "Asiámque" as printed. Coin legends are approximate because the scan is slightly soft at the edges of the medallions.

page.layout: Two oval portrait medallions side by side at the top, centred, each with its legend around the rim (left: TVRC. MOSE.; right: TVRC. IMP. MAHOMETES). Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs. The signature "Nnn" stands at the foot right of the text. A printed ornament lies below, without text. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: TVRC. MOSE.
TVRC. IMP. MAHOMETES
MOSES Orchanem nepotem,cui erat patruus interfecit,
ipse quoque à fratre Mahometo vicissim interfectus est. nec
connumeratur ambo in serie Turcicorum Imperatorum, quòd
paucis admodum diebus imperitarint. Vide Richerium de re-
bus Turcicis lib.i.
MAHOMETES huius nominis primus, Mustaphæ &
Mosis,eius inquam qui Orchanem ex fratre nepotem è medio
sustulerat,frater, post Baiazetem Turcis imperat anno mundi
5359. à Christo nato 1397. Sunt qui ea quæ de Cyriscelebe
feruntur,huic vni tribuant. Is itaque Bulgaros & Valachos præ
dis & cladibus afflixit, tributúmque magnum imposuit. Arma
deinde in Satrapas Asiæ vertit, loca omnia quæ Tamberlanes
occupauerat recepit : nihil generis propinquitate commotus,
Turcicæ nationis complures principes ex Galatia, Ponto &
Cappadocia pulsos extirpauit : alios autem integros atque in-
columes seruauit. Reuersus in Græciam, Adrianopolim, quæ
caput est Thraciæ, sedis imperatoriæ loco habuit, pulsis illinc
Christianis. Obiit anno imperij sui 17. regni verò Caroli hoc
nomine sexti Francorum Regis 35. Vide Richer.lib.i. & Cosm.
Munst.lib.4.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are printed around the portrait rims and are given above as running lines. Doubtful readings: "lib.i." (the numeral may be a small r or i), and "Cyriscelebe" (the printed form is close to Cyri1celebe, with the l hard to separate). The medallion portraits carry no further text. The faint show-through lines below the text are not transcribed.

page.layout: Running head at top, centred: "PROMPTU. ICONUM". Page number top left: 194. Two round medallion portraits with legends, side by side, above the text. One column of text in the centre, two entries, one per paragraph. A decorative ornament below the text, with no printed words.

main_text.l: IMP. SIGIS MVNDVS. AVG.
IMP. ALB ERTVS. AVG.
SIGISMVNDVS, Hungariæ & Bohemiæ Rex, Ven-
ceslai frater, mortuo Alberto communi omnium assensu Im-
perator creatur anno mundi 5372. à Christo nato 1410. Hic
Imperatoriæ planè indolis, sapientia, eruditione, probitate ac
liberalitate clarus, doctos fouit, ac dignitatibus ornauit. Atta-
men ab Amurathe Turcarum principe graui prælio victus, ca-
stris etiam exuitur. Hic per triennium magnam Europæ partem
peragrauit, quò schisma Christiano nomini calamitosissimum
extirparet: quare effecit ut reiectis adulterinis tribus Pontifici-
bus qui Barionæ sedem inuaserat, Od[illegible, ~2 letters]olumnius omnium
consensu Pontifex declararetur. obiit Sigismundus nulla reli-
cta virili prole, cum annos 27. imperasset. Vide Egna.li.3.
ALBERTVS Dux Austriacus, post Sigismundi obitum
Imperator designatur anno mundi 5399. à Christo nato 1437.
Hic Sigismûdi gener cùm esset, post eius obitum hæres regno-
rum Bohemiæ & Hungariâ factus est. Morauos ac Sarmatas in-
tra suos fines quiescere compulit. Bohemiæ factiones compe-
scuit: Amurathe Turcam, qui Hungariâ inuaserat, fugauit: Syn-
derouiam in deditionem accepit: inde in Græciam contendes,
Thessalonicam expugnauit. Austriam repetens, moritur anno
imperij sui (proh dura fata) secundo. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: The ink blot covers part of the word after "Od" in the first entry, so two letters are unreadable and the name is given as illegible. The legends on the two medallions are partly cut off at the edges of the coins. I have copied them as far as they can be read, and the split between the left and right legends is uncertain. The ornament below the text carries no printed words. The running head is printed as "PROMPTV. ICONVM" and has been normalised to u as a vowel.

page.layout: Two medallion engravings at the top, with their legends around the rims. Below them one column of running text, with a paragraph beginning "BEATRICINA". Gathering signature at the foot right.

main_text.l: PHILIPPVS Maria, obtruncato Ioanne fratre supradi-
ćto, armis paternum Mediolanensem inquam ducatum repetit
anno mundi 5379. à Christo nato 1417. Callidus hic in bello
pacem, in pace bellù poscere visus est. Discendi auidus semper
fuit, callidus, sagax, liberalis, in iniuriis relaxandis facillimus,
statura procerus, vultu formidabilis, maturo consilio, arte, ac
validissimis armis, tyrannos qui suae ditionis ciuitates occupa-
rant, è medio sustulit. Recuperauit Comum, Tricium, Berga-
mum, Brissiam, Placentiam, Laudem, Cremonam quoque sub-
egit. Io. Iacobus M[illegible, ~3 letters]ferrati Marchio, veritus huius poten-
tiam, Vercellas, Alexandriam, Astamque sponte Philippo re-
stituit. Suo praeterea dominio Genuam maritimam vrbem po-
tentissimam adiecit. Genuenses itaque subacti, ac eius subditi,
Alphonsum Neapoli, & Io. Nauarrae Reges, & magnum magi-
strum S. Iacobi Compostellani fratres, cum aliis primoribus su-
pra 100. & equitibus clarissimis vltra 200. praelio nauali ceperūt:
quos ad se perductos humanissimè excepit: ac multis donatos
muneribus dimisit: cum illorum regnū ac ditionem totam sibi
vindicare, aut occupare facile potuerit. Tandem foedissima li-
bidine insaniuit, & mutata fortuna, nulla relicta virili prole,
obiit ventris profluuio anno salutis 1447. Vide Paul. Ioui. &
Supplem. Chro. lib. 14.
BEATRICINA, antea Facini Canis vxor, iam vetula,
nupsit praedicto Philippo, & numerauit dotē aureorū 400000.
hanc postea vt suspectam interfecit. Deinde Mariam Amidei
Sabaudiae Ducis filiam in coniugem ductam, praeuentus mor-
te, intactam dimisit. Vide autores quos supra.

page.notes: Engravings: left medallion, profile of Philippus Maria Visconti in a cap, legend "PHILIPPVS M.VI" on the right rim and "COM D MLI" (partly reversed, uncertain) on the left rim. Right medallion, profile of Beatrice (Beatrix) in a veil, legend "PHILL.M.D.M.VXOR" on the left rim and "BEATRICINA" on the right rim. Both legends are part of the engraving, not running text. The dark blot over "Mon..." in "Io. Iacobus Mon-ferrati" hides about three letters; "Mon" is the likely reading but was not read. "Placentiam" is partly obscured by the same blot; the word is read as printed. "Recuperauit" and "Tricium" are as printed.

page.layout: One column of running text, with two medallion portraits with legends at the top of the page. The left medallion has its legend on the left and right sides, and the right medallion has its legend around the top and right. Below them, one column of two entries (AMVRATHES and SCANDERBEGVS), with no margin notes.

main_text.l: MAHVS.R.
AMVR[?]
TVR[?]
DVX EPIRI ALB.
SCANDERBERGVS
AMVRATHES, hoc nomine secundus, Mahometis su-
pradicti filius, patri in Turcarum imperio succedit anno mun-
di 5378. à Christo nato 1414. Hic cognita patris morte, ex
Asia in Thraciam cupiens traiicere, Mustapham patruum cui
Græci fauebant, auxiliúmque ferebant, fundit, ac delet. Primus
pro tuitione corporis, Ianizaros, Christũ abnegantes, instituit,
quorum viribus & ipse, & qui ipsi succedere, totum pene de-
bellarunt Orientem. Is Hungariam, Bosinam, Albaniam, Vala-
chiam & Græciam infestauit: Venetis Thessalonicam ademit.
Ladislaum Poloniæ Regem, & Iulianum Cardinalem, ac Hu-
niadem vicit. Regnat annos 34. Vide Riche. lib.1. Paul. Iou. &
Cosm.Munst. lib.4.
SCANDERBEGVS, siue Scanderbechus, sic dictus
à Turcis inter circuncidendum: antea enim vocabatur Georgius
Castriotus, is inquam à patre, Epiri atque Albaniæ, seu Mace-
doniæ, principe, datur obses Amurathi Turcarum Regi septi-
mo: qui eum tandem post multa egregia facinora, expeditioni,
quam aduersus Hungaros parabat, præficit: porrò ad hos cùm
res malè Turcis cederet, desciscit Scanderbegus, atque à secre-
tario Bassa literas ad Croiæ magistratus extorquet, in quibus
nomine Amurathis, ciuitas ac præfectura sibi tradatur. sic Cro-
iam patriam recipit circiter annum mundi 5409. à Christo nato
1447. Cæterum Amurathes Epirum cum ingenti exercitu repe-
tit: at Croia frustra per aliquot menses oppugnata, mœrore ani-
mi obiit. Vide vt supra. & Marinum Barletium lib.1.

page.notes: Two medallion portraits with legends; the legends are only partly legible at this scan resolution. The left legend's inner words are uncertain and marked [?]. The text shows light show-through from the reverse side, which is not transcribed. The printed "Ladiflaum" and "Theffalonicam" were read with the long s as plain s, and the printed "fecretario" line-break reads as "secretario".

page.layout: Running head top left, page number top right. Two medallion portraits with legends side by side above the text (legends transcribed as lines). Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs. Signature "Nnn 3" at the foot, right. No margin notes, no catchword.

main_text.l: CAROLVS REX FRA.
VII.
LVDOVICVS
XI. FRAN. REX
CAROLVS huius nominis septimus Francorum Rex,
vnicus Caroli sexti filius, patri in regno succedit anno mundi
5384. à Christo nato 1422. Tunc regnum Francicum turbu-
lentissimum fuit, nam Anglorum Burgundionúmque bello pe-
titus Carolus, omnibus pene regni finibus amissis, ad Bituri-
cen-ses se contulit, apud quos mansit: quare ab hoste Bituricen-
sium Rex per iocum dictus est. Henricus sororis Caroli filius
inter titulos, Angliæ, Franciæq; Regem se scribebat: qui etiam
Parisiis in Franciæ Regem coronatus est. Ioanna puella, armis
instructa, militis subit munus: obsessos Aurelianenses iuuat, ho-
stes cogit obsidionem soluere: per loca ab hostibus occupata
Regem Carolum Remis consecrandum ducit, multásque in
itinere vrbes recipit: tandem ab hostibus capta, Rothomagi
exuritur. Lutetia Francorum Armis Angli pelluntur. Pragma-
tica sanctio in concilio Basilienfi ædita, à Rege probatur, & in
Senatu Lutetiæ promulgatur. Vniuersam Normaniam Caro-
lus recuperat: Angli expulsi, præter Calitium & vicina aliquot
loca nil in Gallia possident. Delphinus secundò à patre deficit,
aduersus quem pater bellum mouet, & spoliatum rebus omni-
bus, ne à quoquam excipiatur inhibet: porrò ad Burgundiæ
Ducem ille profugit. Regnat Carolus an.38. Vide Gaguin.li.9.
LVDOVICVS Caroli septimi filius, apud Burgundio-
nes agens, nuntio paternæ mortis accepto, in Galliam cõfestim
transit, ac Francorum Rex creatur anno mundi 5422. à Chri-
sto nato 1460. Bellum geritur, bonum publicum, vulgò dictum,
de quo fusissimè tractat Philippus Cominius, & syncerissimè:
nam huic bello interfuit. Regat Ludo.an.23.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are printed inside the illustrations; the left legend's last word "FRA." is read from a rotated, low-contrast print and is uncertain. Page is slightly blurred at the top left; no other doubtful readings. Printed "Burgundionúmque" keeps its acute accent as printed.

page.layout: Running head at top with page number at left. Below it, two engraved coin medallions side by side, with their legends printed around the rims. Then one column of text with two paragraphs, full width, no margin notes.

main_text.l: IMP. IOANNES
MANVS VII. CONST. IMP. CONSTANTI
IO ANNES, Manuelis Palæologi filij, filius natu maior,
post mortem patris in imperio succedit Constantinopolitano,
circiter annum mundi 5395. à Christo nato 1433. Paci hic ac
concordiæ magis quàm bello studens,comitatus totius Græcię
comitibus, cùm sacris, tum profanis , atque Eugenij huius no-
minis quarti Pontificis autoritatem sccutus[?], Ferrariensi, quod
deinde Florentiam translatum est, concilio interfuit : suscep-
túsque est ab Eugenio Imperatorum more: atque ex duabus,
nempe Græcorum ac Latinorum Ecclesiis, una facta est. Tunc
à Græcis ac Latinis de processione Spiritus sancti damnatus est
error.Reversus Imperator,haud ita diu supervixit. Vide Egna.
lib.2.& Cosmog.Munst.lib.4.Plati.& Volater.
CONSTANTINVS, septimus Manuelis filius, mor-
tuo sine liberis fratre Ioanne supradicto, Constantinopoli im-
perat, circiter annum mundi 5406. à Christo nato 1447. hic
ab initio Peloponnesi Rex,Draconis cognomen inditum acce-
pit, ob eam quam in Turcas exercebat ferocitatem. At verò à
Mahomete Amurathis secundi filio capta Constantinopoli,
ipse Constantinus ad portam trepidus se recipiens,fugientium
trepidatione oppressus obiit:cuius caput pilo affixum,totis ca-
stris ad ludibrium hostis gestauit: anno mundi 5414. à Christo
nato 1452. Id mirum , atque in fatis quasi habendum , nempe
quòd à Constantino Magno Helenæ filio Constantinopolis,
urbs Romæ semper æmula, condita aut instaurata sit, ac sub
Constantino, qui eiusdem nominis matrem haberet, capta,
Turcarúmque iugo ad hanc diem sit subdita. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: Two engraved coin medallions above the text, showing profile portraits of Ioannes (left) and Constantinus (right, with a double-faced or two-headed portrait). The legends around the medallion rims are part of the engravings and are given as the first two lines. Doubtful readings: "sccutus" (the word is possibly "fccutus"; long s is written as s). Printed spelling and printing errors are kept as they stand, such as "Ferrarien-" and "Reuersus" corrected to "Reversus" per the u/v rule, and "superuixit" corrected to "supervixit".

page.layout: One page of text. Above the text, two medallion engravings side by side: left, a profile portrait of Carolus Burgundiae Dux; right, a profile portrait of Bartholomaeus Coleo. Below them, two paragraphs of running text, one for each entry. Gathering signature at the lower right. No marginal notes or foot notes.

main_text.l: DVX KAROLVS BVRGVNDIVS
BARTHOL·CAR[?] LEO·MA·CL[?]·SE[?]
CAROLVS, Philippi Burgundiæ Ducis filius, patri suc-
cedens, bellicosus ac strenuus, bellum gesit aduersus Ludo-
vicum Francorum Regem, huius nominis vndecimum, cum
quo postea fœdere inito, in Leodienses bellum mouit, quos &
debellauit. Nouesium quod alij Nusiam vocant, agri Colo-
niensis oppidum, diu obsedit, hoc est annum integrum. Huc au-
tem maximè spectabat Carolus, vt imperio Diocesim Colo-
niensem adimeret: aduersus hunc expeditionem parat Fride-
ricus Imperator: Tandem fœdus hac conditione ineunt, vt
Maximilianus Friderici filius, Mariam Caroli Ducis filiam vni-
cam, in vxorem accipiat. Pugnauit Carolus semel atque ite-
rum, infeliciter quidem, cum Heluetiis. Cæterum ad Nansen
contra Argentinensium Heluetiorúmque auxiliares copias di-
micans, à Renato Lotaringo victus miserè occubuit, anno
mundi 5437. à Christo nato 1475. Hic antequam pater more-
retur, bellum etiam Gandauis intulerat. Vide Chron. Philippi
Cominij, & rerum memorabilium Paraleipomena.
BARTOLOMÆVS Coglio siue Coleo, Bergoma, cla-
rissima ortus familia, Dux exercitus Venetorum creatus est,
atque à Carolo Duce Burgundionum supradicto, & Ioanne
Andegauensi Duce, per priuilegia autentica in familiis eorum
ascriptus. Hic bellicis artibus instructus, consilio item, pruden-
tia, ac humanitate maximè pollebat: huius etiam aulæ ampli-
tudo, pompa & gloria, omnium ferè principum aulas æquabat.
Videto Supplementum Chronicorum lib.16.

page.notes: The two medallion inscriptions are printed around the engraved portraits; the right-hand one is worn and only partly legible, so its letters are marked [?]. The left-hand medallion reads DVX (lower left) and KAROLVS BVRGVNDIVS (around the top and right). The running head contains no number; the page number 199 is in old-style figures at the top right.

page.layout: Top: page number at left and running head centred. Two engraved medallions side by side, with no text block between them. One centred text column of two paragraphs. Below the text a tailpiece ornament.

main_text.l: CALIXTVS Papa huius nominis secundus, in Pontifi-
cem eligitur post Gelasium huius nominis secundum, anno
mundi 5080. à Christo nato 1118. fuit hic natione Burgun-
dus, frater Ducis Burgundiæ, prius Archiepiscopus Viénensis,
divinarum scripturarum peritissimus, nec ab humanioribus li-
teris abhorrens. Sanctum Iacobum Apostolum coluit: in cuius
honorem Compostellanam ecclesiam in Archiepiscopatum
erexit. Videto Trithemium. præfuit Ecclesiæ in summo Ponti-
ficatu annos ferè sex.
PIVS, huius nominis Papa secundus, creatur Pontifex an-
no mundi 5419. à Christo nato 1457. Hic Æneas Syluius an-
tea vocatus, natione Tuscus, patria Senensis, vir undecunque
doctissimus, Philosophus, Orator, & Poëta insignis, multa do-
ctrinæ ac ingenij sui monimenta posteris reliquit. In concilio
Basiliensi Prælato cuidam minister fuit: deinde in Scribā Can-
cellariæ Friderici Imperatoris, huius nominis tertij, assumptus,
& Poëta ab eo, Laurea recepta creatus, primò Episcopus, postea
Cardinalis, tandem Papa omnium suffragio electus est. Obiit
Anconæ, Friderico, huius nominis tertio, imperante. Videto
ut supra. Pontificatum gesit annos sex.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions above the text, portraits in profile. The left one has the legend "CALISTVS PAPA TERTIVS" (left and right of the head, as printed). The right one has "PIVS II PON MAX." Both legends are part of the engraving and are not transcribed as text. Tailpiece ornament below the text, no printed words. The "Viénensis" accent is uncertain in the scan. The "Scribā" macron and "gesit" spelling are as printed. No catchword, signature or marginal notes.

page.layout: Running head at top with page number at right. Below, two medallion portraits side by side, each with its legend printed around the rim (two lines of legend, no text block). Below them one column of running text with two paragraphs. Gathering signature at the lower right of the text. No margin notes.

main_text.l: PAVLVS
P. M. SAC. CV [?]
IIII. [?]
SALXIS [?]
PAVLVS, hoc nomine Papa secundus, Pio supradicto in
Pontificatu successit, anno mundi 5425. à Christo nato 1463.
Hic Petrus Barbarus antea dictus, Eugenij huius nominis
quarti Pontificis ex sorore nepos, sedit annis ferè 7. corpore
fuit amplo, & maiestatis Pontificiæ digno. Duo bella toto suo
Pontificatu in Italia suscepit.Robertum Sigismundi Malatestę
filium aggressus est. Cæterum pauperum curam gessisse perhi-
betur, imperiosus tamen ac fastu plenus cùm esset, odiosus
omnibus fuit. Eius prima cura fuit, ut quæ victui essent neces-
saria, urbi non deessent. Die quadam cùm iucundissimè coe-
nasset, apoplexia correptus obiit. Vide Chronicorum Supple-
mentum.
SIXTVS huius nominis Papa quartus in locum Pauli su-
pradicti suffectus est, Pontificarumque obtinuit anno mundi
5432. à Christo nato 1470. Hic natione Ligur, ordinis Mi-
norum generalis antea minister,sedit annis tredecim.Hic cùm
alioqui fuisset vitæ pientissimæ, ac in pauperes & religiosos
munificentissimus,attamen suos nimis amavit,eis diuina & hu-
mana contribuens,id est ecclesiastica & temporalia bona,præ-
ter Dei & Romanæ Ecclesiæ dignitatem ac honestatem: &
quædam bella iudicio multorum præter æquum suscepit: im-
primis contra Laurentium Medicen, & Florentinos, quibus
multa damna intulit: & contra Ferdinandum Apuliæ Regem,
dein contra Venetos. Tandem febre correptus, cùm audisset
fœdus ictum inter Venetos & reliquos principes, expirauit.
Hic festa seraphici Francisci, conceptionis & præsentationis
D.Mariæ,& S.Annæ & Ioseph celebrari iussit. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are printed inside the woodcuts; their letters are partly worn and the numerals of the left medallion ("2 PONM 223") and the right ones ("P. M. SAC. CV", "IIII.", "SALXIS") are doubtful. Some words of the text are set with a grave accent (cùm, iucundissimè, cùdm, cùm) which I have copied as seen; a few of these are uncertain. Printed spacing errors kept: "suscepit.Robertum", "minister,sedit", "tredecim.Hic", "amavit,eis", "contribuens,id".

main_text.l: ALEXANDER TARTAGNVS
ANDREAS BARBATIVS[?]
ALEXANDER Targinus de Imola, siue Imolensis, Iu-
reconsultus doctissimus claruit temporibus Friderici Impera-
toris huius nominis tertij, & Sixti Papæ, huius nominis quarti,
de quibus supra mentionem fecimus. Hic Alexander, in usum
eorum qui iurisperitiæ operam dant aliquot libros conscripsit,
quos nominatim descriptos habes apud Ioannē Trithemium.
ANDREAS Barbatias legum peritissimus, multa præ-
clara in iure edidit opuscula, quorum nomenclaturam pores[?]
etiam apud Trithemium legere.

main_text.l: FRIDERICVS III
ROM. IMP.
LEONORA
IMP. FRIDERICI III. UXOR.
FRIDERICVS Austriæ Dux, post Albertum imperat
anno mundi 5401. à Christo nato 1439. hic pacis atque otij
studiosissimus fuit: seditionem mouentes Austriacos facilè
compescuit. bellum à Matthia Pannoniæ inferioris Rege illa-
tum, composuit: in Flandros mouẽs, qui filium Maximilianum
ceperant, & asseruabant, recepto filio paucorum pœna conten-
tus, omnem discordiarum fomitem sustulit. Romæ unà cum
uxore Heleonora, siue Leonora, Lusitani Regis filia, corona-
tus, inde Neapolim ad Alphonsum uxoris necessarium ac san-
guine cognatum, diuertit, à quo, & ab ipsis postea Venetis, sum-
mo honore, & apparatu excipitur. Iterum Romam voti reus pe-
tit, priuati more, atque humili veste indutus: quo voto damna-
tus ad suos redit: & quiescente Germania, moritur anno impe-
rij 53. Maximiliano prius Cæsare designato. Vide Baptistam
Egnatium, Romanorum principum lib.3.
HELEONORA, siue Leonora, supradicta, Lusitaniæ
Regis filia, uxórque Friderici Imperatoris, Romæ cum marito
Imperij corona insignitur anno mundi 5412. à Christo nato
1450: Ex hac Maximilianum, qui postea imperat, sustulit Fri-
dericus. Vide Egnatium ad calcem libri tertij, in Friderici Im-
peratoris supradicti vita.

page.notes: Decorative vignette (scrollwork ornament) at the foot of the page; no text. Two circular medallion portraits of Frederick III and Eleonora; their legends are transcribed above as lines, in the order they appear: left medallion (ROM. IMP. and FRIDERICVS III), right medallion (LEONORA, IMP. FRIDERICI III. UXOR.). The number "53" in the first paragraph is set with a small gap in the scan; read as 53. The line-end "summo" is split across lines ("sum / mo") with no printed hyphen, written whole.

main_text.l: RENATVS
APVRE[?]
IOANNES D.
CALABER
RENATVS Lotaringiæ Dux, Apuliæ Regis ex filia ne-
pos, à Venetis solicitatus spe regni Apuliæ obtinendi, quod sibi
hæreditate materna debebatur, Venetias iuit. Fœdere cum Ve-
netis percusso, in Ferrariensem agrum bellum mouet, atque
urbis ipsius, Ferrariæ inquam, oppugnationem adgreditur. Ve-
rùm ab Alphonso Aragonum Rege fortiter pulsus, cum exer-
citum viribus eneruari, ac se ob aëris intemperiem mala vale-
tudine affici sentiret, inglorius in patriâ rediit, circiter annum
à mundo condito 5404. à Christi natiuitate 1442. hunc per-
hibent fuisse probitatis eximiæ principem, nec à maioribus de-
generasse, qui verè pij, & synceræ fidei cultores semper sunt
habiti. Videto Supplem. Chronicorum lib.16.
IOANNES, Calabriæ ac Lotaringiæ Dux, primogenitus
Siciliæ Regis filius, magnanimus, bellicosus, & æquitatis aman-
tissimus extitit. Videto ut supra.

page.notes: Medallion legends are printed in the engravings; the surnames and the first legend are read clearly. The second word of the left legend is partly cut off and is uncertain. The page number is printed in old-style figures ("2o4"). The running head is printed as "PROMPTV. ICONVM"; the V is a vowel and is normalised to U. The ornament at the foot is decoration only. Long-s is plain s throughout.

main_text.l: FRANCIS SFORTIA DVX [?]
CŌ. D. MILIS GALEAZ MAVI [?]
FRANCISCVS Sforza, Sforzæ à Cutiniola filius, Phi-
lippi Marię Vicecomitis gener, ab eodē adoptatus est, &angue[?],
insigni familiæ donatus, anno salutis 1430. socero defuncto,
proximo statim anno, ob singularem virtutem Mediolani prin-
cipatum adeptus est. Hic Sforzæ cognomen à Sforza patre bel-
licofo traxit: qui humilis & abiectus, cum se militiæ tradidiffer,
per vim ab aliis quicquid cuperet extorquebat, sicque Sforzæ
cognomen assecutus, vt proprium nomen semper postea habuit,
& ad posteros cognomen trānsmisit. Hic per cunctos gradus, ad
summum militiæ culmen conscendit. Contra Eugenium Papam,
contra Florentinos, Venetos, Mediolanenses, non semel victor,
Guelforum, ac Gibellinorum nomen ferè è medio tulit, Italiæ
vniuersæ propemodum factus terror. Composita cum Venetis
pace, multæ Italiæ ciuitates eius exēpla secutæ, arma deposuere.
Intus forisque pacatis omnibus, à fundamentis denuò erexit
castrū Mediolani, quod Iouis dicitur, à populo antea dirutum.
Magnum illud hospitale, ægrotis recipiendis, ædificauit, quod
regali censu ditauit, opus in orbe rarum. Vt diui Ambr. têplum
erigeret, multum auri expendit. Tandem verò hic tantus vir,
adeò libidine exarsit, vt adolescentum flagitia superarit. rexit
an. 16. obiit, sex filiis duabúsque filiabus relictis, anno salutis
1466. Vide Supplem.lib.15. & Archie. Antonium.
GALEATIVS Maria, Francisco Sforzæ patri defuncto,
statim in Mediolani principatu succedit, pulsa matre quæ rem
cum eo administrabat: multis hic se inquinauit flagitiis: quam-
obrem adulteriis, homicidiis, incestibus, sacrilegiisque pollu-
tus anno administrationis 9. liberis 4. relictis, in æde Diui Ste-
phani vulneribus est confossus. Vide Supplem.Chron.

page.notes: Medallion legends are engraved, not set type; the two lines above are read from the curved inscriptions and are doubtful, especially the ends of each line (DVX, MAVI, CŌ. D. MILIS). The "&angue" reading in the first paragraph is doubtful. Faint show-through of the reverse page is visible below the text and was left out. A small mark "1" stands at the bottom centre; it is not clearly a gathering signature and was left out. The text has no catchword.

page.layout: One page of text. At the top, two medallion engravings side by side, each with its legend around the rim: left "MAHOMETES" (right side) and "IVTVRC. IMP." (left side); right "BAIAZETES" (right side) and "TVRC. IMP." (left side). Below them, two paragraphs of running text in one column, with no margin notes. Page number top left; running head top centre.

main_text.l: IVTVRC. IMP. [?]
MAHOMETES
MAHOMETES, hoc nomine secundus, Turcarũ verò
Rex octauus, Amurathi, etiam huius nominis secūdo, succedit
anno mundi 5411. à Christo nato 1449. Hic regnum à parri-
cidio auspicatur. fratrem paruulum, ne pater solus sepeliretur,
opera Mosis interficit. Impiissimus nullum Deum credidit: Ma-
hometem suum, Pseudoprophetam sui similem dixit: Prophe-
tas ac Patriarchas risit, ac nugas duxit: huic tametsi impio, fauit
aliquando fortuna. Nam magni cognomentum Othomannicæ
familiæ quæsiuit. Duo Christianorum imperia Constantinopo-
litanum & Trapezuntinum subuertit: regna 12. ademit: ducen-
tas urbes Christianas cepit: Ipse colico dolore correptus, quar-
to demum die moritur, anno ætatis 58. regni 31. Richer. lib. 4.
Paul. Iou. Egna. lib. 2. Cosm. Munst. lib. 4.
BAIAZETES hoc nomine secundus, Mahometis supra-
dicti filius Ianizarorū opera Turcis imperat anno mundi 5442.
à Christo nato 1480. Hic minorem fratrem Zizimum, quem
primores Imperatorem exposcebat, vincit ac fugat: qui à Rho-
di praefecto ad Carolum octauum in Galliam mittitur. Porrò
Baiazetes Caramanno fuso, quaecunque is cis & trans Taurum
Turcis ademerat, recepit: Valachiam subegit: In Sultanum Æ-
gyptium mouit: Sed is potentior, vtpote qui Mamaluchos, post
Caramanni cædem fugitiuos exceperat, ac Arabum maximas
copias ad sui tuitionem alebat, Baiazete sæpe debilitat, ac pro-
fligat: postea Cerauniorum montium accolas subdit. Venetis
Methonem, nunc Modonem, Nepathum, olim Naupactum,
& Dyrrachium ademit. Acomathem primogenitum decrepitus
Baiazetes absentem in locū suum substituit: Sed, Ianizaris Zeli-
mo suffragantibus, cogitur pater Zelimum pro Acomathe sub-
stituere. paulò post imperio deturbatus à filio Zelimo, ab eodē
filio veneno necatur, anno regni 30. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: Medallion legends are read from the engravings; "IVTVRC. IMP." is uncertain, and the right legend may read "TVRC. IMP.". "eodē" at a line end: the macron over the e is faint, so it is uncertain. The numbers 1 and 4 in "Richer. lib. 4." and "regni 31." are slightly blurred. A faint show-through line lies between the two paragraphs and is not transcribed. The small-capital openings MAHOMETES and BAIAZETES are kept as printed.

page.layout: One page of text. At top, under the running head, two medallion portraits with circular legends (left: Sigismundus Malatesta; right: Robertus Malatesta). Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs, with no notes in the margins and no catchword.

main_text.l: SIGIS. MAL. TE
ROBER. MALATE NOTHVS [?]
SIGISMVNDVS Malatesta Arimini princeps, Pandul-
phi Malatestæ filius spurius, bellicosus admodum, splendidus
& liberalis fuisse perhibetur: interim tamen multis flagitiis in-
quinatus turpi nota nomen suum inussit: ideoque diris & armis
Pontificum obnoxius fuit. Hic tres duxit uxores, primam Cri-
mignolæ comitis filiam, quam mortuo patre repudiauit: cum
tamen dotem ex ea amplissimam percepisset: Secundam Nico-
lai Estensis, Ferrariæ principis filiam, generosam ac probam:
hanc nihilominus paulo post veneno sustulit: tertiam Francisci
Sfortiæ filiam, præclaram & modestam, quam tandem propriis
etiam manibus, ut mensuram scelerum suorum impleret, ap-
prehenso ac fortiter presso iugulo suffocauit. Vide Supplem.
Chron. lib. 15.
ROBERTVS Malatesta Sigismundi filius, etiam nothus,
patri in principatu Ariminensi succedit, anno mundi 5428. à
Christo nato 1466.Fuit hic moribus patri dissimilis, belli etiam
artibus, & præclaris rebus gestis ornatissimus. pro Venetis, sub
quorum stipendiis diu militauit, varia mortis pericula adiit.
Cum Galeatio Mediolanensium Duce, & Florentinis suas copias
iunxit, & oppida omnia quæ Pontifex patri in Arimi-
nensi agro ademerat recepit. Hic Alfonsum Calabriæ Ducem,
alioqui fortissimum vicit, ac fugauit: quo in bello, præ ardore
pugnæ nimio, in dysenteriam incidit, nec ita diu, hoc dolore
correptus, superuixit. habuit in uxorem Elisabetam, Vrbini
Ducis filiam. Vide ut supra.

TE" (the second word may be MALATESTA, cut by the circle), the right reads "ROBER. MALATE" and "NOTHVS" along the rim. "Cri-mignolæ" and "Sfortiæ" are read from the scan with the printed line-end hyphen kept. Print shows "1466.Fuit" with no space, kept as printed.

main_text.l: DVX MII[?] SP[?]
IO GZ MAS SFORZ[?]
M DVCES MELI[?] VI[?]
BONA GZ[?]
IO. MARIA, patre, ab Andrea à Lāpognano, interem-
pto, à Senatu populóq; adhuc paruulus Mediolanensium Dux
creatus est anno mundi 5438. à Christo nato 1476. Bonæ ipsius
matri & consanguineis quibusdam, atque primoribus, regimi-
nis cura commissa. Hic inter vivendum ac moriendum infeli-
cissimus fuit. Nam tutores brevi Bonam à gubernatione repel-
lunt: & Ludouicus patruus atque tutor, arte & astu principa-
tum invadit, permittens adolescentem à virtutibus deflectere,
& voluptatibus operam dare. Nec prius hic tantum suum ma-
lum advertit, quàm cùm morti esset vicinus, hausto iam vene-
no quod ei pararat patruus. Itaque hoc pacto, cum annos 26.
mensésque 9. Ducem nomine tantùm egisset, inglorius diem
clausit extremum, Francisco Sforza secundo, filio relicto, ex
Isabella Ferdinaldi Neapolis Regis filia suscepto. Morti eius ac
funebri pompæ Christianissimus Carolus Galliæ Rex, qui
Neapolim tunc petebat, interfuit. Vide Supplem. lib.16. & Ar-
chie. Antoni.
BONA, Sabaudiæ Ducis filia, inter omnes Heroides lau-
datissima, Galeatij Mariæ olim uxor, peperit illi quatuor libe-
ros, duos mares, totidemque fœmellas. Hæc Io.Gal.Mariæ filio
adhuc parvulo tutrix à viro moriente relicta, parùm admodùm
in administratione perseveravit, à Ludouico Sforza, Mauro vo-
cato, adolescentis patruo, & tutore deturbata, ac in ordinem
redacta. Vide autores quos supra.

page.layout: Two portrait medallions side by side at the top, with their inscriptions; below them one column of text in two paragraphs; right below the text the signature mark "Ooo"; at the foot a woodcut tailpiece. Running head at the top, page number at the top right.

main_text.l: FRANC·ACCOLTIVS AR.
CEPOLA VER. BARTOLEMÆVS
FRANCISCVS Aretinus Jurisconsultus excellens mul-
ta scripsit studiosis mirum in modum utilia, super Digesta, Co-
dicem, & Decretales. Scripsit etiam Consilia, de Differentia
inter sententiam interlocutoriam & definitiuam. Magnum no-
men adeptus est per universam Italiam, præsertim in florentibus [?]
Academiis, ut Patavi, Bononiæ, & aliis. Erat valde amatus à suis
Discipulis, qui eum in quamuis Academiam migrantem, eius
studio incensi, semper sequebantur, ut in Jure magis proficeret.
Florebat anno salutis humanæ 1469. Vide Conradum Gesne-
rum, in sua Bibliotheca.
BARTHOLOMEVS Cepolla Veronensis doctissimus
Jurisconsultus fuit, numero celebriorum sui temporis ascriptus,
maximè in practica Juris, ut videre licet ex magno volumine
ab eo conscripto & hoc titulo nominato, Cautelæ causarum
Ciuilium. Scripsit etiam volumen consilorum criminalium:
Tractatum de seruitutibus: alium, De Ædilitio edicto, de Præ-
diis urbanis, De prædiis Rusticorum, De re militari, De furtis,
De Imperatore militum, De simulatis Contractibus, & plures
alios, si [?] per jus ciuile & criminale. Floruit anno salutis 1477.
Vide Conradum Gesnerum, in sua Bibliotheca.
