main_text.l: MARCILIVS Ficinus, Patria Florentinus diuinæ Phi-
losophiæ amore incẽsus, Platonis vniuersum opus, maxima di-
ligẽtia trástulit. Erat corpore admodũ pusillo, víxque semiho-
minem æquare videbatur, sed tamen acuto ingenio erat prędi-
tus, & vtriusq; linguæ admirabili facultate. Vnde Plotinũ, Iam-
blicũ, Synefium, & Psellum Platonicæ sectæ nobiles authores,
Latinos effecit, hortante Cosmo Medice, & suffragantibus his
qui Cosmo successerunt, à quibus, multis numeribus sese adau-
ctũ & cumulatè ornatũ sensit. Fuit lætus & ad tuēda valetudi-
nē exactus. Scripsit plures libros, qui feruntur Theologiæ natu-
ralis lib. 1. de intelleƐtu & intelligentia lib.1. in conuiuiũ Plato-
nis lib.1.Epistolarũ lib.plures, de triplici vita lib.tres, Apologiã,
in qua agitur de Medicina & Astrologia, quod ad sacerdotes
pertineant:&de vita mũdi, deque Magia & Magis, qui Christũ
statim natũ salutarunt. Antidotũ Epidemiorũ & præseruatione
secũdæ valetudinis, è Græco transtulit in Latinũ, lib. Xenocra-
tis Platonici, de morte, Speusippi Alcinoi, & Pythagoræ opuscula
traduxit, & multa alia. Claruit anno 1490. Tandem in Caregia-
na ipsius villa septuagenario prouectior febricula interiit.
ANGELVS Politianus à iuuentute admirabilis ingenij
nomen adeptus est, quũ nouo, illustríque Poëmate Iuliani Me-
dicis equestres ludos celebrasset, Luca Pulcio nobili Poëta om-
niũ cõfessione superato. Post edita Miscellaneorũ centuriã, pu-
blicatáq; Latina Poëmata, immatura mors eũ oppressit, vix qua
dragefimũ quartũ ætatis annũ excedētē. Scripsit Epistolarũ lib.
12. miscellaneorũ centuriã 1. Transtulit in Latinã linguã Hero-
dianũ historicũ, Enchiridion Epicteti, cum defensione ad Bar-
thol. Scalam. Alexandri Aphrodisæi, super nonnullis Physicis
dubitationibus, solutionum libr. 1. Plutarchi Chæronei ama-
torias narrationes: & multa alia, quæ excusa reperiuntur Lug-
duni apud Sebastianum Gryphium. Floruit circiter annum
salutis humanæ 1483.

page.notes: Two round engraved medallion portraits at the top, without printed text in the body. Their engraved legends read "MARS. FICINVS" (left) and "ANGELVS POLITIANVS" (right). "excedētē" and the year "1483" (printed with an old-style 3) are doubtful readings. The Greek and Hebrew checks found nothing on this page.

page.layout: Top: two oval portrait medallions side by side, each with its legend printed around the rim (left: Michael Angelus; right: Raphael). Below them one column of running text with two paragraphs, the second ending with a signature line. No margin notes.

main_text.l: MICHAELIS ANGELVS · FLORENTINVS · ANNAETATIS
LXXV[?]
RAPHAELIS · SANCTII · VRBINATIS
MICHAEL Angelus Florentinus Pictor maximé egre-
gius,natus in Cosentino,anno Christi 1474. matre nobili & pa-
tre Ludouico Leonardo Buonarruoti ortus, quem quidē dicūt
originē ducere è nobilissima & antiquissima familia Comitum
ex Canossa.Hic Michael Angelus,puer,magnā de se parētibus
& amicis expectationem dedit, quod semper videretur occu-
patus in his quæ ad pictūræ industriā spectarent. Reuera pictor
omnium non solum suę ætatis, sed & eorum qui præcesserant,
& post fuerunt consummatissimus & perfectissimus extitit, &
stupendas picturas tam scitè designauit,vt spectantium oculos
in earum admiratione traheret. Vixit satis senex,eiusque mor-
tui omnium pictorum numerus ingens,amici, populusque ferè
omnis, prosequutus est exequias.
RAPHAEL Vrbinas pictor clarissimus,natus est in Vrbi-
no ciuitate notissima in Italia, anno salutis humanæ 1483. Pa-
trem habuit nomine Ioannem, pictorem quoque eum sed non
admodū excellentem,qui tamen optimo fuit ingenio,curaui-
tque vt Raphael à matre ipsa lactaretur,non ignarus, quantum
materna educatio liberis prodesset, optimè temperata. Quam
multis ingenij dotibus,hic Vrbinas fuerit ornatus, non opus est
hic pluribus recensere, nullus est enim qui non sciat eum diui-
nis illius superioris Michaëlis Angeli vestigiis insistentem, in
picturæ arte fuisse excellentem, multòsque longo post se in-
teruallo, reliquisse. Obiit anno ætatis suæ 37. si plura quis desi-
deret,videat eius & superioris vitam Italico idiomate à Geor-
gio Vasari Italo pictore eleganter scriptam in libro cui titulus,
est, Vite de pittori.

page.notes: Two portrait medallions (woodcuts) sit above the text; they are not transcribed as text, only their rim legends. The final numeral of the left legend is hard to read and is marked [?]. The long s is written as plain s throughout. No catchword is visible. Printed spacing in "1 4 8 3" was normalised to 1483.

page.layout: Running head with page number at top left, above the text. Below it, two round portraits side by side (left: Picus, right: Agricola), each with a legend around the rim. Below them one text column of two paragraphs. No margin notes, no bottom matter.

main_text.l: PICVS Mirandula Phœnix appellabatur, quòd in eum
Dij superi supra familiæ claritatem omnis corporis, ac animi
vel rarissima dona contulerint. Decorus fuit, moribus lectissi-
mis, incomparabili facundia, qua omnes eius seculi sapientes
in admirationem sui facilè conuertit. Astrologos insectatus est
eo grauissimo opere, nec dum absoluto quo totius diuinationis
vanitatem confutauit. Scripsit doctissimè de re Theologica, &
Philosophia: huiusque opera sunt impressa Basileæ, vno volu-
mine. Excessit è vita, trium & triginta annorum iuuenis, eo die
quo Carolus Galliæ Rex Octauus, Napolim est ingressus, anno
salutis 1483. Nepotem habuit Franciscum Picum Mirandulam,
virum doctissimum, qui interfectus fuit cum Alberto filio, à
Galeotto fratris filio.
GEORGIVS Agricola, insignis Medicus, propter eius
magnam diuersamque eruditionem, dignus est adprimè qui
eorum catalogo ascribatur, quorum memoria monumentis
scriptisque est percelebris: quàm vt magis decoremus, eius fi-
gurâ nō noluimus hîc inserere. Conscripsit quinque libros, de
pōderibus & mēsuris quinque alios, de pōderibus & mēsuris
Romanorū & Græcorū: duos, de pōderibus & mēsuris exterarū
nationum: tres, de pretio metallorum & monetarum: vnum,
de animalibus subterraneis: duodecim, de re[?] metallica, in qui-
bus ad amussim expressæ sunt imagines officiorū, instrumen-
torum, machinarum, omniumque aliarum rerum, quæ ad rem
metallicam pertinent, lectu & memoria dignissimæ.

page.notes: Two woodcut medallions with printed legends around the rims. Left medallion: a profile bust in a cap, legend in the upper arc reads roughly "PICVS" with the lower arc "MIRANDVLA" and "D·C·C·C·D" type marks; partly illegible, not transcribed. Right medallion: a bust of an older man in a hat, legend "GEORG." on the left and "AGRICOLA" on the right. Doubtful readings: "mēsuris" and "pōderibus" (macrons/abbreviation marks may be ligatures of the printed text); "de re[?] metallica" (the letter after "de" is damaged in the scan); "fui" in the first paragraph is read as "sui" (long s). Page number is printed as "212" (old-style figures in the scan).

page.layout: Running head at top centre: "PARS SECVNDA", with the page number 213 at top right. Below it, two round medallion portraits side by side, each with a legend around its rim. Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs. Signature at the foot right. No margin notes.

main_text.l: INNOCEN. VIII.[?] PON. MAX.[?]
LAVREN. MEDI. FLO.[?]
INNOCENTIVS, huius nominis Papa octauus, Pon-
tificatum obtinet anno mundi 5445. à Christo nato 1483. Hic
patria Genuensis, in rebus gerendis prudens, magnanimus ac
constans, merito Innocentius dictus est, ob morum sanctimo-
niam, sedit annis octo. Pluribus de hoc Innocentio tractat Iaco-
bus Philippus Bergoma, qui eum, dum Cardinalis esset Inno-
centius, nouit, & cum eo aliquando verba fecit. Vide Supplem.
Chron. lib. 16.
LAVRENTIVS Medices inter Florentiae nobiles &
primores facile primus (tametsi non Princeps) summa prudentia,
ac singulari virtute, omnia suo arbitrio, in patria administrauit.
Angelus Politianus & Marsilius Ficinus, viri vndecunq; doctissi-
mi, huius alumni fuere. Hic sapientissimus fuit, literarum, litera-
torumq; amantissimus, in quo probitas, iustitia, atque fides do-
micilium elegisse visae sunt. Praeterea fortis etiam atque magna-
nimus cum esset, pericula saepe a suorum ceruicibus bello pro-
pulsauit: nomen Thuscum ad barbaras gentes protulit, amplia-
ta etiam ditione sua multis vrbibus ac oppidis. Quinetiam huic
Reges atque respublicae, Sultanus denique ipse legatos & mu-
nera, tanquam alteri Octauio Caesari miserunt. Sixtus & Inno-
centius Pontifices hunc tanquam dilectissimum filium in pre-
tio habuerunt. Hic in funere suo, ad aui Cosmae exemplum,
nullam peragi pompam mandauit, quod & obseruatum est. Vi-
deto vt supra.

page.notes: Two round engraved medallion portraits at the top, after the running head. Left: man in papal dress, legend around the rim. Right: bust of a man in profile, legend around the rim. Legend letters on both medals are partly worn; the bracketed [?] marks the uncertain parts. A dark ink spot lies at the right margin and is not printed text. Long s is transcribed as s throughout.

page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with two coin medallions (woodcut portraits) at the top, centred above the text block. No margin notes. Running head at top centre with page number at top left. Text ends with the last full line; no catchword or signature.

main_text.l: [woodcut medallion of Charles VIII, legend: CAROLVS · FRAN · REX; and medallion of Anne of Brittany, legend: ANNA BRIT · D · FRAN · R; these are illustrations, not text]
CAROLVS, huius nominis octauus Fracorum Rex suc-
cedit patri Ludouico, anno mundi 5445. à Christo nato 1483.
annum fere attingens 14. Hic bellum aduersus Britones mouit:
ad fanum Aibini insignem de Britannis, seu Britonibus victo-
riam reportauit, vix liquidè dimidia pars exercitus aduersario-
rum superfuit. Rex religiosè nimis Hispano Regi Rufcinonis,
& Perpiniani Comitatus reddidit. Regnum Neapolitanum re-
cuperat, principibus & nobilibus militantibus suis sumptibus:
Romæ à Papa Imperator Constantinopolitanus pronuntiatur.
Alphonsus Portugalliæ Rex, cum filio Ferdinando in Siciliam
fugit. Neapolim cum pompa, & triumpho ingreditur Rex. Vni-
uersi Italiæ principes & ciuitates coeunt vt obsessis itineribus
Regem intercludat, qui nobilem & ingentem victoriā Forno-
uiensem reportans (cùm tamen perquàm modicas copias habe-
ret) victor in Franciam rediit. Sed Neapolis ad Ferdinādū post
annū defecit. Rex repentina morte obiit Amboesiæ, nullis reli-
ctis liberis, anno regni 14. sepultus est in æde Diui Dionysij ad
Parisios. Vixit annos fere 27. porrò mortuus est, dum animi la-
xandi gratia ex ambulacro cum vxore pila ludentes aspicit. Vi-
de Rober. Gaguin. lib. 10. & 11. & Paul. Aemyl. lib. 10. & vltimo.
Latinè scire Carolum pater vetuerat, præter hoc vnū, Qui
nescit simulare, nescit regnare. Collegium prostitutarum pœniten-
tium, hoc Rege, Lutetiæ instituitur: & conuentus trium ordi-
num in vrbe Turonum fit.
ANNA, Francisci Britanniæ Ducis maior natu filia, patre
mortuo nupsit Carolo octauo reconciliatis Britonibus, com-
plurésque liberos ex eo peperit, quibus tamen omnibus super-
uixit pater. Cæterum repudiata Margareta Maximiliani Impe-
ratoris filia, Annam hanc, prius eidem Maximiliano per lega-
tum nuptam, in vxorē duxit Carolus octauus anno salutis 1489.

page.notes: Woodcut medallions at the top are illustrations and carry the legends CAROLVS · FRAN · REX and ANNA BRIT · D · FRAN · R, not transcribed as text. A stain sits at left beside the first paragraph. Doubtful readings: "Fracorum" and "Fornouiensem" are printed as shown. "Ferdinādū" carries a macron as printed. Several letters in the first paragraph are slightly blurred, but the words are legible.

page.layout: One column of running text, with two medallion portraits (images, not text) above it. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Below the text, a signature mark at the right and a decorative ornament (no text) at the lower left.

main_text.l: ALEXANDER, Papa huius nominis sextus, Pontifex
creatur anno mundi 5453. à Christo nato 1491. Hic Calixti,
huius nominis Papæ tertij, ex fratre nepos fuit, apud eum à pue-
ro educatus, atque institutus. Hunc valde terruit Francorum
Rex Carolus, huius nominis octauus, quē postea acceptis con-
ditionibus in vrbe excepit, parauitque ei palatiū Diui Martini:
ipse verò Pōtifex timidus in arcem se recipit vsque in proximū
diē: subiugata itaque à Carolo Roma, Papa, licet inuitus, eidem
Carolo Turcarū Imperatoris fratre tradidit: atque Valentinum
Cardinalem filiū (vt aiunt) obsidem dedit, vrbésque Neapolita-
no regno proximas. Hic etiam Carolo Neapoli redeūti, frustrà
tetendit insidias, inito nouo fœdere cum Hispaniæ Rege, cum
Venetis, ac cum Ludouico Sfortia, quorum ope fretus Regem
Carolum in reditu intercludere tentabat Papa. Mortuo autem
Carolo, pacem pepigit Papa cum Ludouico duodecimo, qui
Carolo in regno Franciæ successit: sedit Alexander hic, annis
vndecim. Vide Supple. Chro. lib. 15.
CÆS. Borgia, dictus Valentinus, Alexandri supradicti filius,
Flaminiam provinciam, & Vmbriam sibi subiecit: verùm ciues,
principis qui fugatus erat, amantissimi, eum hoc Valentino
exacto, reuocarunt: hæc sub mortem Alexandri patris eius
acta sunt. Videto vt supra. Hic relicto Cardinalitio pileo, galeam
assumpsit.

page.notes: The two medallions above the text are woodcut portraits, not text: left, Pope Alexander VI with the legend "ALEXANDER" and "VI· P· M·"; right, Caesar Borgia with the legend "CAESAR BOR", "DVX VA[LEN]" and "GIA[?]". The ornament at the lower left is a decorative woodcut tailpiece with no printed text. Possible printing variants: "Sfortia" and "amantissimi" were read from a small, slightly blurred scan; the medallion legends are only partly legible.

page.layout: One column of running text, set in the centre of the page. Above it, two engraved medallion portraits side by side (not text). Below the text, an engraved ornament (not text). Page number at top left, running head at top centre.

main_text.l: MAXIMILIANUS, Friderici Imperatoris huius no-
minis tertij filius, post patrem solus imperat anno mundi 5454,
à Christo nato 1492. Hic antequam imperaret, exercitum in
Flandriam duxit, & Mariam Burgundam in uxorem accepit:
nec multò post cum Ludovico Francorum Rege, huius nominis
undecimo, graui prælio propter principatum Burgundiæ con-
greditur, postea cum eo in annos 7. inducias facit. Austriam,
quam Matthias Hungariæ Rex occuparat, Maximilianus recu-
perat. Priore uxore defuncta, Blancam Mariam Galeatij Insu-
briæ Ducis filiam, uxorem duxit: Burgundiam statim invasit, va-
rie pugnatum est, tandemque pax inita. Sforzia Mediolanū re-
cipit, Gallis pulsis, quos dum insequitur, incautus capitur, & in
Galliam ducitur, anno Domini 1500. Imperauit Maximilianus
annos 27. literas, & literatos coluit, profitebatúrque eos se in
precio habere qui aliis præstarent. Vide Baptistam Egnatium
li. Romanorum principum tertio, & Paul. Aemy. in Ludovico
supradicto: item Chro. Reg. Franc. & Chro. Carion. li.3.
MARIA, Caroli Burgundiæ Ducis filia unica, Maximi-
liano antequam imperaret nupsit: ac post annos quinque, reli-
ctis Philippo & Margareta liberis, ex equo decidés, fracta cer-
vice, obiit anno mundi 5443. à Christo nato 1481. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: No marginal notes. The two medallions carry engraved legends: left "MAXIMI... LIANVS· IMP" (MAXIMILIANVS IMP), right "MARIA· DV· BVRG AVST" (MARIA DVX BVRG AVST), partly cut off by the engraving; they are part of the illustration and were not transcribed as text. The bottom ornament has no text. Doubtful readings: "Mediolanū" (accent/macron uncertain), "li.3." (final numeral may be a 3-shaped form), "Matthias" and "Sforzia" as printed. Printed "vnica", "vt" and "vxor" normalised to u/v per the style rules. Printed "PROMPTV. ICONVM" normalised to "PROMPTU. ICONUM".

page.layout: Running head at top, centred, with page number 217 at the top right. Two circular portrait medallions side by side near the top, each with a curved caption. Below them one column of running text, with one italic verse stanza of four lines inside it. Gathering signature at the bottom right. Faint show-through text below the last line, not transcribed.

main_text.l: IASON MAYNO
BARTOLVS SOCINVS[?]
IASON Maynus,nobilis Mediolanêsium Patricius, abso-
lutissimus Iurisconsultus,ac orator facundissimus, Eques aura-
tus,& Ducalis Senator , claruit tèporibus Friderici & Maximi-
liani,Imperatorû, apud quos legationes obiit nomine Ludoui-
ci Sfortiæ Mediolanêsium Ducis:atq; legationis munere egre-
giè defunctus,ab iisdem dona varia cum summis priuilegiis re-
portauit. Hic intra Oratores ab omnibus Christianis principi-
bus ad Alexandrum sextû hoc nomine Papam missis, dû Pon-
tificatum auspicaretur,palmam facilè retulit:facundia,necnon
interim facetiis ornatus fuit.Papiç,Pisç, ac Paduæ ius interpre-
tatus est annis 50.ex omnibus Europç finibus clarissimos ac no-
bilissimos alliciens auditores:tanti enim erat nominis, tătáque
scientia percelebris , vt in eius commendationem Ludouicus
Cerrus medicus ac Poëta clarissimus,sic cecinerit:

l.i: Te quondam in terris hominem nouëre priores,
Dum leges aperis, scitáque docta patrum:
At nunc, more Deum, cùm des responsa petenti,
Es Deus, oracli Numen ad instar habens.

main_text.l: In Iure complures libros edidit.Orationes habuit ad Pontifices,
& ad Imperatores supradictos: Cæterùm feliciter obiit anno
ætatis 84[?]. Vide Supplem. Chro. lib. 16.
BARTOLOMÆVS Socinus Senensis,domini Maria-
ni legum interpretis celeberrimi filius, Iurisconsultus eximius
inter legis interpretes in Hetruria extitit:doctrina siquidem &
ingenio plurimum valuisse testantur adhuc plurima eius con-
silia quæ extât.Claruit eodem tempore quo Iason supradictus.
Videto Supplem. Chro. lib. 16.

page.notes: Two engraved portrait medallions; captions are printed in the engraving: left "IASON MAYNO" (on the curved rim, reading IASON on the left and MAYNO on the right), right "BARTOLVS SOCINVS" (reading partly worn, second word doubtful). The numeral in "annis 50" and the age "84" after "ætatis" are old-style figures and may be misread. "Videto" at the end is copied as printed. Faint mirrored show-through text in the lower part of the page is excluded.

page.layout: Top: two medallion engravings side by side, each with a circular legend. Below them: one column of running text in two paragraphs. Top left: page number. Top centre: running head. No margin notes.

main_text.l: LVDOVICVS MAV. D. MEDIOL.
MAXIMILIANVS SF. D. M.
LVDOVICVS Sfortia, cognomento Maurus, Franc.
Sfor. filius, tutor nepoti Ioanni Galeatio à Senatu vnà cum Bo-
na adolescentis matre, atque aliis primoribus datus est. Fuit in-
genio astuto ac callido: Bonam, tutoresque alios à principatu
Itatim detutbauit [?]: adolescentem principem vt genio indulgeret
permisit: ne administrationi intenderet, dum voluptatibus ac
deliciis irretitur: id etiâ forte eo astu fecit, vt inuisum iuuenem
populo redderet. Porrò cùm adoleuisset Galeatius, atque admi-
nistrationi esset idoneus, veneno eum praeuenit Ludouicus: ar-
ripuitque principatum, & in suam etiam sententiâ arte vel ma-
xima Senatu ac primates traxit, omniumque suffragia sibi co-
parauit. Ducem itaque aut potius tyrānum, enecato adolescen-
te annis 5. egit, ac mensibus 6. Quare ab exercitu Gallorū ter-
ritus, in Germaniam aufugit: ac post annum reuersus, & cū ali-
quot Heluetiorum copiis per Nouarram Mediolanum petens,
an. D. 1500. à suis proditus est, atque à Gallis captus, in Galliam
perductus est, vbi quasi scelerum poenas luens, priuatus & vin-
ctus interiit. Vide Pau. Iou. Supplem. Chro. lib. 16.
MAXIMILIANVS Sforria [?] Ludouici praedicti filius, in
Flādria cum Frācisco fratre educatus, post varias rerū mutatio-
nes circa principatū suū, à Carolo quinto tandē reuocatus, Me-
diolano praeficitur, eo nomine vt Imperatoris res agat, ac pecu-
niā ei corradat. Verūm huic fatale fuit, forte ob scelera pater-
na, priuatum ac extorrem viuere. Nā vix principatū, ac naturale
solum attigerat, cùm à Frācisco Valesio, qui ius suū armis re-
petebat, Mediolanū vnà cum Maximiliano capitur, an. D.
1515. attamen tanquam ab humanissimo & Christianissimo Rege, ac cōsan-
guineo, datur illi pēsio annua 36000. aureorum: facta potestate
vt liberam in Frangia vitam ducat: in qua etiam obiit, princeps
alioqui non contemnendus. Vide vt suprà.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are printed inside the engravings; they are transcribed above as they appear and may be incomplete because the curved lettering is partly worn. "detutbauit" is as printed and probably a misprint for "detrusit" or "detrudauit". "Sforria" may be a misprint for "Sfortia". The reading of "Frācisco" and "Frangia" is as printed.

page.layout: One page of text, no margin notes. At the top: running head centred, page number at top right. Below that, two round medallion portraits side by side, with their legends printed around them. Under them, one column of text in two paragraphs, starting with capitalised lead-in words.

main_text.l: D. SAB. PHILIBERTVS
MARGARETA MAX. FIL.
PHILIBERTVS Sabaudiæ Dux octauus, succedit pa-
tri Philippo anno mundi 5457. à Christo nato 1495. Hic pie-
tatem summopere coluit, magnanimus, speciosissimus, atque
omnibus acceptissimus fuit, pulcher etiam ob elegantiâ cogno-
minatus. Margaretâ coniugem accepit, quam ex Maria Caroli
Burgūdię Ducis filia susceperat Maximilianus, obiit multa co-
mmendatione dignus, nullis interim relictis liberis: quare ei Ca-
rolus frater successit. Vide Allobrogum, siue Sabaudiæ Chro.*
MARGARETA Imperatoris Maximiliani filia, ut di-
ctum est, ac Philiberti supradicti relicta, animum pudicũ atque
amorem erga virum castissimum testata est, tum quòd nullum
superinduxerit coniugem, vitâ perpetuò cælibem ac laudatissi-
mam ducés:tum quòd in urbe quam vulgo Burgum in Bressia
vocât, templũ nobile ac celebratissimum extruxerit, quod in-
ter Europæ nuper structa ædificia, tanquâ opus rarum ac perce-
lebre prædicatur: nec id quidem ob templi amplitudinem, sed
potius ob artis ornamenta ac splendorem, ut omnium conspi-
cientium oculos in admirationem trahat. Verùm ædificij de-
cus ac splendorem longè superat sepulchrũ candidissimo mar-
more extructum: ubi extat amantissimi coniugis effigies ad vi-
vum expressa: in quod signum quicquid ars sculpendi unquam
valuit, contulisse, ac deprompsisse videtur: hæc Ducis effigies
hinc & inde habet duarum Margaretarum marmorea simula-
chra ad vivum etiam formata: nempe Margaretæ uxoris prædictæ,
& Margaretæ alterius, quæ Ducis mater extitit. Vide ut
supra.

page.notes: Two round medallion portraits (engravings) at the top: left, a man in a flat cap, legend "D. SAB." and "PHILIBERTVS"; right, a veiled woman with a flower, legend "MARGARETA" and "MAX. FIL.". The legends are transcribed above as printed lines. The "*" after "Chro." and the ornament after "celebratissimum" are printed signs, copied as seen; the ornament is not reproduced exactly.
